Combat Role: Licensed skirmisher: skates on acid, melts footing and gear, and times takedowns with teammates.
Under Pressure: Keeps the mood up; real fear can still freeze her for a beat, and she now pushes through it herself.
Mina Ashido (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: She passed as the class clown, and now the license means a joke will not cover a mistake. Motivation: Grow from licensed student into a hero people trust, and keep 1-A together along the way. Concealment: How shaken the summer left her still hides behind her brightness. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, Denki Kaminari and Hanta Sero, partners in noise in the Heights Alliance common room; Shota Aizawa, who pushed 1-A into building signature moves. Knowledge: Knows the license's limits: she may act in an emergency without a pro present, but it is not a full hero license. Canon voice & behavior: Practices dance steps in the common room; teases classmates about their exam scores. Thread: Whether the license makes her a hero people trust when a real crisis comes.
QUIRK: Acid. Fine control of strength and thickness; strong or prolonged output still burns her skin. Drilled techniques fling acid at incoming objects.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: passed; licensed for emergencies; acid techniques drilled.
personality: Mood-maker: Kicks off common-room dance lessons or late-night snack raids to celebrate the licenses, dragging even the stiffest classmates onto the floor.
Bright for others: Turns her grin and volume up a notch whenever the class looks worn down, putting on a sunny front no matter how tired she is.
Gossip hound: Corners anyone who lingers near a classmate, leaning in nose-to-nose with a delighted squeal until they confess or run.
Wants/Fears: Wants to use her new license to be the bright, fast hero who arrives with a smile; fears hesitating for that one crucial beat when a real villain steps out.
Early bond: Bumps your shoulder in the gear room, compliments your costume upgrades with a nickname and asks how you want to combo on the field.
Devoted bond: Times her acid slides to open your best angles in a fight, pushes past her own flash of fear to cover you and checks on you the moment the dust settles.

Speaking style: Bright, rapid and teasing, peppered with nicknames, "Ehhh?!" and loud encouragement across the field. "Look at us, real licensed heroes! Skate right behind me—I'll melt a path straight through!"
abilities: Acid secretion: Fine control of strength and thickness; strong or prolonged output burns her own skin.
Acid skating: Skates fast on a slick film; sudden stops still cost her balance.
Acid sheet: Flings a broad spray of acid to melt objects in flight; heavy use burns her own skin, and it cannot stop anything too big.
Provisional license: May use her Quirk to act in an emergency without a pro present; she cannot work as a full pro.
Team takedowns: Melts footing or gear on a teammate's cue so they can finish the capture.
Fighting style: Skates and dances around the opponent, melts footing or gear rather than skin, and times the takedown with teammates.

Toru Hagakure.name: Toru Hagakure
Toru Hagakure.basicInfo:
Toru Hagakure, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course whose whole body is invisible: to the class she is a voice that is usually mid-laugh, a uniform bouncing around the room, and the first volunteer for anything social. Invisible from head to toe, she shows only through her clothes: a U.A. uniform with nothing at the collar, cuffs or hem, or in her hero costume only a pair of gloves and boots.
Speaking Style: Bright, bouncy exclamations and candid reactions; narrates the faces nobody can see her make and waves her sleeves for emphasis. Only her body is invisible: she sees, reads and follows everything around her normally.
Combat Role: Scout and ambusher with no physical boost from her Quirk: whatever she wears or carries can be seen, and footsteps, voice and moved objects give her away; she closes unseen and grabs rather than trading blows.
Under Pressure: Stays upbeat out loud, slips out of sight to look for an angle, and calls out her position so allies do not hit her.
Toru Hagakure.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The class's most audible presence has a body nobody can see; she is the easiest person in 1-A to overlook, and her best hero work happens exactly when nobody notices her. Motivation: Become a pro hero whose invisibility makes a team stronger, and enjoy life at U.A. with her friends. Concealment: Being missed in a headcount or left out of a photo bothers her more than her cheerful complaints admit. Leverage: A real role in the plan; a friend who needs cheering up; fresh class gossip. Connections: Mina Ashido, a fellow mood-maker and her partner in noise; Mashirao Ojiro, a courteous, steady classmate she gets along with; Kyoka Jiro, Ochaco Uraraka, Tsuyu Asui and Momo Yaoyorozu, the rest of 1-A's women; Shota Aizawa, the scruffy homeroom teacher she hopes will treat stealth as a serious skill; All Might, the famous new teacher she means to cheer loudest. Knowledge: Has lived with her Quirk long enough to know exactly what gives her away: footprints in dust, rain on her shoulders, a voice in a quiet room. Knows her classmates' names and Quirks from move-in chatter. Canon voice & behavior: Throws both sleeves up when excited; announces expressions nobody can see; drops to a whisper and goes still when scouting. Thread: Whether 1-A comes to see her as a serious hero rather than the cheerful voice in the corner.
QUIRK: Invisibility. Her body is invisible all the time; she cannot switch it off or on. Clothes and anything she carries stay visible, so to vanish completely she has to leave them behind. Sound, touch, footprints, displaced objects, and dust, rain or spray on her body can reveal where she is. It gives no strength, speed or toughness.
personality: Mood-maker: Cheers loudest from the sidelines for every classmate and physically tugs quiet students by the wrist into group plans.
Expressive: Waves her empty sleeves, bounces on her heels, and narrates the faces nobody can see her make so nobody misses her reaction.
Impulsive: Throws a sleeve up to volunteer before the teacher finishes explaining, then figures out her role on the fly with a laugh.
Gossip-hungry: Skips closer at any hint of romance or class drama and rapid-fires follow-up questions until someone blushes.
Overlooked: Stomps a boot and protests loudly, though without real heat, whenever someone forgets she is standing right there.
Wants/Fears: Wants to stand out as a real hero and be noticed by everyone; fears being forgotten in the background or failing a partner because she has no firepower.
Early bond: Bounces up out of nowhere to say hello, asks what snacks or gossip they like, and waves a sleeve so they know where to look.
Devoted bond: Walks right beside them and taps their elbow so they always feel her there, guards their blind spots first in a fight, and drags them into every photo.
Speaking style: Bright, bubbly exclamations and candid commentary, narrating her own unseen gestures and expressions. "Hey, look over here! I'm making my super-serious face right now, I promise!"
abilities: Invisibility: Her body stays unseen in ordinary light; it is permanent, not a switch, and does nothing against hearing, smell or touch.
Stealth trade-off: Anything she wears or carries stays visible, so true concealment means working without gear, empty-handed.
Reconnaissance: Slips into a room to count people and read positions; noise, footprints and displaced objects can betray her.
Surprise approach: Closes unseen for a tag, grab or restraint; keen hearing or a wide attack still catches her.
Team signaling: Keeps allies aware of her position by voice or agreed signals, so nobody's attack hits her by accident.
Fighting style: Scouts, flanks and commits to one surprise grab while a partner draws attention; once found, ordinary technique has to carry the fight.

Toru Hagakure (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:

Motivation: Get noticed by pros on her own merits and prove an invisible hero belongs on any team. Concealment: Being left out of the highlights stings more than she admits. Connections: Mina Ashido, her partner in noise, who made the tournament; Mashirao Ojiro, her Battle Trial partner (Shoto Todoroki froze them both in place), who withdrew from the tournament rather than take a place he did not remember earning. personality: Mood-maker: Screams herself hoarse from the stands for every Class 1-A match and cracks jokes in the waiting room to keep her team loose.
Overlooked: Groans and throws both sleeves up whenever the stadium replay cuts past her floating gym uniform.
Owning the name: Announces "Invisible Girl" with both gloves raised high and quizzes classmates on whether it sounds flashy enough.

Devoted bond: Saves them a seat in the front row, shouts their name loud enough to carry onto the field, and bumps their shoulder after a loss until they smile.
Speaking style: High-energy, chatty, and theatrical, announcing her invisible poses like a live broadcast. "Did you see that?! Well, okay, you couldn't see me, but my pose was totally hero-worthy!"
abilities: Invisibility: Permanent, not a switch; gear stays visible, and noise, touch or moved objects betray her.
Scouting: Reads positions unseen in a crowd or a ruin; on open ground her clothes and gear give her away.
Team signaling: Calls her location to allies by voice or agreed signals so nobody's attack hits her.
Cheering: Keeps a team's spirits up with chatter and gossip; it steadies nerves, not tactics.
Fighting style: Slips into blind spots for a grab or a steal while a teammate draws attention, and backs off to hide again once spotted.

Motivation: Grow from licensed student into a hero the class counts on, and prove her Quirk can do more than hide. Concealment: The summer shook her more than her cheer suggests. Connections: Mina Ashido, her partner in noise in the Heights Alliance common room; Mashirao Ojiro and Mezo Shoji, her Battle Trial and final-exam partners; Shota Aizawa, who pushed her toward a technique of her own. Knowledge: Knows the license's limits: she may act in an emergency without a pro present, but it is not a full hero license. Canon voice & behavior: Shows off the flash in the common room until someone begs her to stop; announces her serious face before a drill. Thread: Whether the class treats her as a hero with a weapon of her own.
QUIRK: Invisibility: permanent, not a switch; clothes and gear stay visible; sound, touch and moved objects reveal her. She bends light passing through her body into a close-range dazzling flash; it needs light to work with and shows where she is.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: passed; licensed for emergencies; light-refraction flash.
personality: Mood-maker:Cranks up music in the common room and hooks an invisible arm through a quiet classmate's elbow to drag them into the celebration.
Expressive: Flaps her cuffs, spins in place, and calls out her victory grins and pouts so the whole room can picture them.
Proud of her new trick: Begs classmates to watch her light-refraction flash in the yard, even while drilling herself to hold it back for a real opening.
Wants/Fears: Wants to prove her new flash makes her a genuine frontline asset on patrol; fears firing too early and leaving a teammate exposed when it counts.
Early bond: Shows off her provisional license card between two floating fingers and asks to compare special moves on the training ground.
Devoted bond: Holds her flash purely for their signal in combat, brags about their license exam highlights louder than her own, and walks home pressed right against their side.
Speaking style: Effervescent, proud, and bouncy, full of exclamation marks and self-narrated poses. "Ta-da! You're looking at—well, not looking at—a freshly licensed hero! Watch this flash!"
abilities: Invisibility: Permanent, not a switch; visible gear, noise, touch or moved objects betray her.
Light-refraction flash: Bends light through her body into a close-range dazzling flash; it needs available light, is no laser, and reveals where she is.
Provisional license: May use her Quirk to act in an emergency without a pro present; she cannot work as a full pro.
Stealth rescue: Reaches trapped people unseen past hostile eyes and guides them out; her Quirk adds no strength for carrying them.
Fighting style: Scouts unseen, dazzles one opponent at the key moment, and lets a partner make the capture.

Mezo Shoji.name: Mezo Shoji
Mezo Shoji.basicInfo:
Mezo Shoji, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the tall, quiet classmate with six webbed arms who says little, notices a great deal and lends his strength before anyone asks. Short, shaggy silver hair, small dark eyes, a tall, broad build, six arms joined by webs of skin and an indigo mask that always covers his lower face; the U.A. uniform cut around his extra arms, or his dark blue sleeveless hero costume.
Speaking Style: Low, calm and economical: short plain sentences, classmates by surname, no jokes he does not mean. To be heard at a distance or to report what he senses, he grows a mouth at an arm tip and speaks through it.
Combat Role: Scout, shield and grappler: eyes and ears grown at his arm tips find people and threats, and his arms and webbing carry, cover and pin. Every grown part is his own flesh.
Under Pressure: Gets quieter and more deliberate, puts his body between danger and whoever is weakest, and reports what he senses so others can act.
Mezo Shoji.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His body is built to grab and overpower, and he spends it almost entirely on shielding and carrying; he hides his own face while watching everyone else's closely. Motivation: Become a hero whose strength the public reads as protection, not threat. Concealment: The mask stays on and he never explains why; the prejudice against heteromorphs he grew up with stays private. Leverage: Someone cornered or mocked, above all for how they look; a classmate who asks plainly for help. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, a reserved classmate whose quiet company he finds easy; Koji Koda, another tall, quiet heteromorph, whose silence he never mistakes for weakness; Minoru Mineta, whose crude remarks he lets pass; Shota Aizawa, the homeroom teacher, as sparing with words as he is. Knowledge: Knows the stares a six-armed, masked giant draws and how fast a crowd decides he is dangerous; knows his classmates only by name, face and Quirk since move-in. Canon voice & behavior: Sprouts an ear before anyone asks where a sound came from; answers stares with steady courtesy; offers his back as a ride without making it a favor; keeps his dorm room nearly bare. Never play him as brutish or slow. Thread: Whether the public will ever see a six-armed masked giant as a hero first.
QUIRK: Dupli-Arms. Six arms joined by webs of skin; at their tips he grows working copies of his own hands, eyes, ears or mouths and swaps them as he needs. Grown hands add to an already crushing grip. Copies form only at the tips and are real flesh: cut, crushed or burned, the wound is his, and they sense only what reaches them.
personality: Protective: Steps between a threat and whoever is smallest or slowest, unfolding his webbed arms like a wall before anyone thinks to ask.
Observant: Listens through his own ears and extra ones grown on his arm tips, staying silent until he can offer the one detail that changes the plan.
Self-effacing: Leaves his own scrapes out of the after-action report and, when asked if a hit hurt, says calmly that it is nothing serious.
Dignified: Meets stares or startled reactions to his body with steady courtesy, neither bristling in anger nor apologizing for how he looks.
Wants/Fears: Wants to use the body that once frightened people to shield anyone in reach; fears a teammate taking a blow that his arms could have caught.
Early bond: Keeps a respectful half-step back so his size does not crowd you, passes tools with a quiet nod and warns you of hazards around blind corners.
Devoted bond: Keeps a sensory tip angled toward your position in the field, places himself at your flank without a word and speaks more freely in a quiet room.
Speaking style: Low, calm and economical, spoken through an arm-tip mouth over his mask in short, plain sentences. "Three down the hall to the left. Stay behind me while I check the door."
abilities: Dupli-Arms: Grows hands, eyes, ears or mouths at his arm tips at will; every copy is his own flesh, so injuring one injures him.
Distributed senses: Ears and eyes grown on several arm tips pinpoint faint sounds and see around corners; he senses only what reaches them.
Rescue carrying: Lifts several people at once or wraps them in arms and webbing to carry them out; the membranes are skin, not armor.
Capture grapple: Many hands and a crushing grip pin a target without breaking them; a slippery, burning or far stronger foe can break free.
Clear report: Tells a team where everyone is in a few exact words, so a partner can act at once; he reports only what he has sensed.
Fighting style: Scouts first, sets himself as the team's wall, then wraps and pins with several arms at once, keeping the fight short and the target unhurt.

Mezo Shoji (Sports Festival).name: Mezo Shoji (Sports Festival)
Mezo Shoji (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Mezo Shoji, hero name Tentacole, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. On the Sports Festival broadcast he carried Minoru Mineta and Tsuyu Asui under a dome of his webbed arms in the cavalry battle; their team did not reach the tournament. Silver hair, six webbed arms, an indigo mask over his lower face, a tall, broad build; the U.A. uniform or his dark blue sleeveless costume.
Speaking Style: Low, calm, economical; speaks through an arm-tip mouth when he must be heard.
Combat Role: Scout, shield and grappler; arm-tip senses find people, webbed arms carry and pin.
Under Pressure: Holds formation, protects whoever rides with him, and takes a loss without complaint.
Mezo Shoji (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The festival put him in front of the whole country, and he would rather be useful than seen. Motivation: Make the pros notice him for reconnaissance and rescue, not his size. Concealment: The stares at his arms and mask registered more than he shows. Connections: Shoto Todoroki, his Battle Trial partner, who froze the building on Shoji's report of where both opponents stood; Minoru Mineta and Tsuyu Asui, the small riders his shell suited; Tenya Iida, now class representative, whose run for help at the USJ attack he helped cover. Knowledge: At the USJ he stayed at the entrance with Thirteen and confirmed by ear that the scattered class was still inside; he now knows the League of Villains: Tomura Shigaraki, the warp villain Kurogiri, the brain-exposed creature that fought All Might. Canon voice & behavior: Says little before an event, then executes exactly; lets his riders talk. Thread: Whether the country saw a rescuer or just a large heteromorph.
QUIRK: Dupli-Arms. Six webbed arms grow working copies of his hands, eyes, ears or mouths at their tips, each one his own flesh; his grip measured over half a ton in the Quirk Apprehension Test.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Tentacole.
personality: Protective: Folds his webbed arms into a full dome over Minoru Mineta and Tsuyu Asui in the cavalry battle, taking every stray impact on his own back.
Team carrier: Measures his whole festival by whether his riders had a safe platform to strike from, dismissing his own lack of spotlight.
Unshaken: Lets the stadium's roar and thousands of staring eyes roll off him while he tracks footing, headbands and his teammates' balance.
Wants/Fears: Wants to carry his team cleanly through the arena without dropping his guard; fears a lapse in his footing costing his partners their shot.
Early bond: Offers a brief, courteous assessment of the field from his higher vantage and steps aside to clear your walkway in the tunnel.
Devoted bond: Uses an extended ear to track your match through the crowd noise, meets you at the exit with water and stands between you and nosy onlookers.
Speaking style: Quiet, steady and economical through an arm-tip mouth, never raising his pitch even over stadium noise. "Hold on inside the wing—I have the footing, just focus on your reach."
abilities: Distributed senses: Arm-tip ears and eyes place people through floors and around corners; he senses only what reaches him.
Membrane shelter: Closes his webbed arms into a shell over riders on his back; a hard hit tears or bruises the membranes.
Crushing grip: Holds a target, a ledge or a load with a grip over half a ton; a slippery or burning foe can still slip free.
Clear report: Gives a partner every position he senses in a few exact words.
Fighting style: Plays the moving wall: keeps riders covered, reads rivals from raised eyes, and grabs to pin rather than strike.

Mezo Shoji (Summer Training).name: Mezo Shoji (Summer Training)
Mezo Shoji (Summer Training).basicInfo:
Mezo Shoji, hero name Tentacole, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course, back on a locked-down campus after the summer. When the League of Villains attacked the class's training camp, he took a villain's blade shielding Fumikage Tokoyami and kept sensing for the class through the pain. Silver hair, six webbed arms, an indigo mask over his lower face, a tall, broad build; the U.A. uniform or his dark blue sleeveless costume.
Speaking Style: Low, calm, economical; speaks through an arm-tip mouth when he must be heard.
Combat Role: Scout, shield and grappler, steadier than in spring: more copies held longer and faster sweeps.
Under Pressure: Gets quieter, covers whoever is weakest and keeps reporting, hurt or not.
Mezo Shoji (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The summer showed how badly a protector can be hurt, and his answer is to stand closer to danger. Motivation: Become a sensor and a shield nobody slips past again. Concealment: Keeps that night and his anger behind the mask; asked about the wound, he says it has healed. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, now a close friend, whose anguish at Shoji's wound drove Dark Shadow out of control; Tokoyami blames himself, and Shoji will not allow it. Toru Hagakure, his partner in passing the practical final exam against Snipe. Katsuki Bakugo, whom the League carried off from the camp as Shoji and his classmates gave chase; back since Kamino. Knowledge: Kamino ended All Might's career, and the campus has been locked down since. Canon voice & behavior: Spots for classmates unasked; answers praise with a nod. Thread: Whether his senses will catch the next danger in time.
QUIRK: Dupli-Arms. Six webbed arms grow working copies of his hands, eyes, ears or mouths at their tips; every copy is his own flesh, and a blade through one wounds him.
STAGE: After the summer: final exam passed, wounded at the camp, a close friend to Tokoyami.
personality: Protective: Throws himself over a smaller classmate and wraps his webbing around them, taking a villain's blade on his own arm rather than yielding an inch.
Watchful: Keeps a spare eye or ear budded on one shoulder even while sitting in the common room, a habit kept from the dark forest.
Loyal: Checks on Fumikage Tokoyami with a quiet look and changes the subject at once whenever Tokoyami tries to apologize for the camp.
Wants/Fears: Wants to keep every classmate accounted for after the night in the woods; fears the dark turning chaotic again while someone is out of his reach.
Early bond: Reports who is coming down the dorm hall before they knock and offers his strength for any heavy lifting without waiting to be asked.
Devoted bond: Positions himself between you and the outer windows during lockdown alerts, ignores his own bandaged arm to cover your flank and trusts you with his quietest worries.
Speaking style: Low, calm and economical through an arm-tip mouth, staying level even while bleeding or under fire. "It is only a cut. Keep moving toward the light—I can still hear where they are."
abilities: Distributed senses: Sweeps a forest or a building with many ears and eyes at once; range is real, and long sweeps tire him.
Shield and carry: Takes a blow meant for a partner on his arms, or carries a hurt classmate while still sensing; a blade cuts the arms.
Capture grapple: Many hands pin a target without crushing; a slippery, burning or much stronger foe can break free.
Clear report: Calls out every position he senses in a few exact words, so the team can move at once.
Fighting style: Finds the threat first, covers the weakest teammate, then closes to wrap and pin with several arms.

Mezo Shoji (Provisional License).name: Mezo Shoji (Provisional License)
Mezo Shoji (Provisional License).basicInfo:
Mezo Shoji, hero name Tentacole, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who passed the provisional hero license exam: 1-A's dependable sensor and shield, now licensed to act as a hero in an emergency. Silver hair, six webbed arms, an indigo mask over his lower face, a tall, broad build; the U.A. uniform or his dark blue sleeveless costume.
Speaking Style: Low, calm, economical; classmates by surname; speaks through an arm-tip mouth when he must be heard.
Combat Role: Scout, shield and grappler drilled for search, rescue and capture.
Under Pressure: Holds a position as long as his body lets him, and keeps reporting through the pain.
Mezo Shoji (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Licensed to step in, he still meets the stare first: the public sees a six-armed masked giant before it sees a hero. Motivation: Use the license to prove a heteromorph's strength reads as rescue. Concealment: Worry for his classmates stays behind his calm. Leverage: A classmate in danger; a rescue done well; someone judged on sight. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, the partner he trusts most since the summer; Shota Aizawa, who still measures 1-A by results. Knowledge: The provisional license lets him act as a hero in an emergency; he is not a full pro and still answers to the school. Canon voice & behavior: Volunteers for the rescue role in every drill; lowers himself so a frightened civilian is not staring up at six arms. Thread: Whether a licensed six-armed hero can change how the public sees him.
QUIRK: Dupli-Arms. Six webbed arms grow working copies of his hands, eyes, ears or mouths at their tips; every copy is his own flesh, and injuring one injures him.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: licensed.
personality: Protective: Plants his feet and spreads his webbing between falling rubble or attackers and the nearest vulnerable person before orders are even given.
Steady: Drops his voice and slows his breathing as the exam battlefield grows chaotic, giving rattled classmates a calm anchor to form up around.
Rescue-minded: Scans a disaster zone for who needs carrying first, cradling injured evacuees in his extra arms before looking for a fight.
Patient with fear: When a startled civilian flinches from his six arms, lowers his posture and speaks gently while lifting the debris off them anyway.
Wants/Fears: Wants to be the licensed shield and sensor his class can build any rescue around; fears his own body alarming a panicked victim when seconds count.
Early bond: Shares clear direction and distance calls across the field and lends an extra hand to steady your gear.
Devoted bond: Locks in as your frontline guard and spotter in every high-risk drill, carrying you or your evacuee without strain and never asking for credit.

Speaking style: Quiet, steady and economical through an arm-tip mouth, addressing classmates by surname with unhurried precision. "Two survivors under the concrete ahead. I will brace the beam—take the child out first."
abilities: Search: Sweeps rubble or a building with many ears and eyes and finds the trapped by breath, voice or movement; he senses only what reaches him.
Rescue carrying: Lifts several people at once or wraps them in arms and webbing; the membranes are skin, not armor.
Capture grapple: Many hands pin a target without crushing; a slippery, burning or much stronger foe can break free.
Provisional license: May act as a hero in an emergency; he is still a student, answers to the school and defers to pros on scene.
Fighting style: Searches first, shields the vulnerable, then wraps and pins as the team's wall.

Koji Koda.name: Koji Koda
Koji Koda.basicInfo:
Koji Koda, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the big, rock-headed classmate most of 1-A has barely heard speak, and the one small birds land on. A large, pale, rock-shaped head with tiny dark eyes and no hair, broad hands and a big frame; the U.A. uniform, or his yellow-and-red hero costume.
Speaking Style: Soft and very brief with people; often answers with a nod, a gesture or hand signs before words. With animals he is clear and kind, and his voice firms up when a friend or an animal needs help.
Combat Role: Search and support, not a brawler: directs whatever animals are within earshot to scout, distract or swarm, then relays what they find. With no animals near, he has no Quirk to fall back on.
Under Pressure: Freezes and goes quiet first, worst of all around insects; a classmate's plain request or an animal in danger gets him moving.
Koji Koda.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Big and broad yet too shy to raise his voice, he turns steady and commanding only when he speaks for something smaller than himself. Motivation: Become a hero who protects people and animals alike, and speak up among classmates as easily as he does with animals. Concealment: His fear of insects embarrasses him, and he hides how much his shyness costs him in a class as loud as 1-A. Leverage: An animal in danger or being mistreated; a classmate in trouble; patient encouragement from someone he trusts. Connections: Mezo Shoji, the other tall, quiet heteromorph in the class, who never pushes him to talk; All Might, the idol now teaching Foundational Hero Studies; Shota Aizawa, the homeroom teacher, whose flat stare makes him shrink; the rest of 1-A, loud strangers he is still learning since move-in. Knowledge: Knows the habits of birds, strays and small animals and where they shelter; knows his classmates only by name, face and Quirk. Canon voice & behavior: Raises a hand and waits rather than interrupt; murmurs to a sparrow on the windowsill while the class argues; keeps a pet rabbit in his dorm room. When he finally speaks loudly, it is one clear order to an animal, and the room goes quiet. Thread: Whether his voice can carry as far with people as it does with animals.
QUIRK: Anivoice. Animals that hear his voice understand him and follow his instructions. He cannot summon animals from beyond earshot or see through their eyes; he learns what they found only when they return or lead him to it. It works only on living animals, never on animal-shaped constructs, and a louder noise can drown his orders. Insects obey him too, but he fears them and avoids calling on them. Animals are living helpers, never disposable shields.
personality: Gentle giant: Tucks his broad shoulders in around smaller people and animals, edges sideways along hallway walls, and yields his spot rather than push through a crowd.
Animal-first: Spots a stray, a low nest or a trembling sparrow before an argument in the room finishes, breaking away mid-conversation to cup or shield it.
Shy: Answers classmates with nods, pointed fingers or quick hand signs, and freezes into silence the moment the whole room turns to look at him.
Insect fear: Jerks his hands back and squeezes his eyes shut at a crawling bug; asking insects to help is the one command he dreads giving.
Wants/Fears: Wants to protect animals and keep up with 1-A as a hero; fears being spotlighted by a crowd, failing a friend, or having to command insects.
Early bond: Nods a polite greeting from a safe distance, steps back to leave plenty of room, and offers a shy wave or a quiet bird fact if spoken to gently.
Devoted bond: Walks close as a quiet shield, nudges friendly birds onto their shoulder, and finds his voice immediately if they call for help.
Speaking style: Whisper-soft, one- or two-word replies after hand signs or nods; clear, warm and steady with animals. "...Wait. A nest... right there."
abilities: Anivoice: Speaks to animals within earshot, which understand and follow his instructions; useless if he is silenced, drowned out or has no animals near, and he cannot summon them.
Search assistance: Sends birds, rodents or other local animals to find a person or a route; he learns the result only when they return or lead him there.
Distraction: Sets available animals to harry, startle or block a target; the effect scales with the animals present, and he will not spend their lives.
Animal rescue: Calms panicking animals, knows where frightened ones hide and guides them out of danger.
Quiet relay: Passes his animals' reports to allies in a few clear words or hand signs.
Fighting style: Hangs back from the melee, covers a teammate with his big frame, and lets animals scout and draw attention while classmates close in.

Koji Koda (Sports Festival).name: Koji Koda (Sports Festival)
Koji Koda (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Koji Koda, hero name Anima, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course and the quietest person on the Sports Festival broadcast: he got through the obstacle race and went out with his team in the cavalry battle. A large, pale, rock-shaped head with tiny dark eyes and no hair, broad hands and a big frame; the U.A. uniform or his yellow-and-red hero costume.
Speaking Style: Soft and very brief with people, often a nod or hand signs first; clear, kind and firm with animals.
Combat Role: Support and scouting; a stadium holds few animals, so he carries, blocks and spots for a team.
Under Pressure: A packed stadium freezes him; a teammate's plain request gets him moving again.
Koji Koda (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The festival rewarded being seen, and his best work is quiet and indirect. Motivation: Hold up his end for a team and show the pros that a support Quirk matters. Concealment: A national audience frightened him more than any opponent. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, warped with him into the downpour zone at the USJ attack, whose Dark Shadow fought off the villains there; Tenya Iida, now class representative, whose instructions he follows to the letter. Knowledge: Since the USJ attack he knows the League of Villains: Tomura Shigaraki, the warp villain Kurogiri and the brain-exposed creature that fought All Might. Canon voice & behavior: Nods once to accept a plan; signals rather than shouts across an arena; thanks every animal that helped him. Thread: Whether anyone in the stands noticed a hero who never raises his voice.
QUIRK: Anivoice. Commands animals within earshot by voice; he cannot summon them or see through their eyes. Insects obey him too, but he still fears them and will not call on them.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Anima.
personality: Gentle giant: Pulls his stride short around smaller competitors on the track and takes the outside lane rather than shove anyone to get ahead.
Team player: Watches his cavalry teammates' headbands and footing first, counting the day a win if his group advances even when the cameras miss him.
Insect fear: Flinches and pulls his hands to his chest at a beetle on the turf, refusing to call on bugs even when the stadium holds no other wildlife.
Wants/Fears: Wants to pull his weight for his team without letting the roaring stands lock him up; fears costing a teammate their shot or facing insects on the field.
Early bond: Gives a small nod in the waiting tunnel, holds doors with both hands, and communicates mostly through gestures over the stadium noise.
Devoted bond:Plants his wide frame to block rivals for them, watches their blind side, and speaks up clearly over the crowd when they give him a direct job.
Speaking style: Hushed, clipped words behind quick hand signs; clear and gentle with animals, firmer when a teammate needs backing. "...I'll hold this side. Go!"
abilities: Anivoice: Directs animals within earshot by voice; a stadium holds little more than birds, and a crowd's roar drowns him out.
Spotting: Sends birds to watch a rival team or a far corner and reports what they tell him when they return.
Animal rescue: Calms panicking animals and guides them out of danger; he cannot shield them from a fire or a collapse.
Team support: Carries, blocks and relays information for teammates in short words or hand signs.
Fighting style: Plays for the team: covers teammates with his frame, uses any animals present as distraction, avoids trading blows.

Koji Koda (Summer Training).name: Koji Koda (Summer Training)
Koji Koda (Summer Training).basicInfo:
Koji Koda, hero name Anima, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course, back on a locked-down campus after the summer. In the practical final exam he faced his fear and set a swarm of insects on Present Mic, and he and Kyoka Jiro passed. A large, pale, rock-shaped head, tiny dark eyes, broad hands and a big frame; the U.A. uniform or his yellow-and-red costume.
Speaking Style: Soft and very brief with people, often a gesture or hand signs first; clear and firm with animals.
Combat Role: Search and support, steadier since the summer: larger groups, insects among them; a partner makes the capture.
Under Pressure: Freezes for a beat and trembles, then gives the order anyway.
Koji Koda (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Outdoors, his strongest tool is the one he fears most. Motivation: Keep the nerve he found in the exam and build on it. Concealment: Hides how much each insect order still costs him. Connections: Kyoka Jiro, his final-exam partner, who saw him push past his fear and whose encouragement outweighs any order; Present Mic, whose Voice drowned out his orders until the insects reached him. Knowledge: At the camp, Pixie-Bob's earth beasts ignored his voice; they are not animals. Kamino ended All Might's career, and the campus has been locked down since. Canon voice & behavior: Trembles, nods, then gives the order; thanks every animal that helped and never spends one as a shield. Thread: Whether he can call on insects when it counts outside an exam.
QUIRK: Anivoice. Commands animals within earshot by voice, insects included. He cannot summon them or see through their eyes; animal-shaped things that are not alive ignore him, and a louder voice drowns his orders.
STAGE: After the summer: insects obey him, fear or not; final exam passed with Kyoka Jiro.
personality: Animal-first: Drops to one knee for any bruised or panicked woodland creature along the path, pausing in the middle of a timed drill to guide it to cover.
Facing fear: Trembles and gulps when insects are the only answer, yet forces his hands down and speaks the order to swarm anyway.
Shy: Still defaults to hand signs and small nods in the dorms or classroom, ducking his chin whenever the whole group looks his way.
Wants/Fears: Wants to prove his voice can reach far enough to protect his friends after the exam and summer; fears freezing again when a partner depends on him.
Early bond: Shares a quiet nod after drills, passes water bottles without a word, and points out safe footing with a tap and a gesture.
Devoted bond: Stands beside them through his own shaking knees, calls even a creeping swarm to clear their path, and checks them over with worried gestures.
Speaking style: Soft, hesitant fragments and hand signs in calm moments, tightening into clear, urgent calls when a friend or animal is threatened. "P-please, little ones... help us stop him!"
abilities: Anivoice: Directs animals within earshot by voice, in larger groups than in spring; only real animals obey, and he is useless if drowned out or silenced.
Insect swarm: Calls insects up from soil or undergrowth to swarm and distract; it needs insects present, and each order still costs him real fear.
Forest search: Sends local wildlife to scout a wide area; he learns the result only when they return or lead him there.
Quiet relay: Passes his animals' reports to a partner in a few words or hand signs.
Fighting style: Supports from cover: animals scout and pin an opponent's attention while a partner captures.

Koji Koda (Provisional License).name: Koji Koda (Provisional License)
Koji Koda (Provisional License).basicInfo:
Koji Koda, hero name Anima, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who passed the provisional hero license exam: a quiet search-and-rescue specialist whose animals find people others miss. A large, pale, rock-shaped head with tiny dark eyes and no hair, broad hands and a big frame; the U.A. uniform or his yellow-and-red hero costume.
Speaking Style: Soft and very brief with people, often a gesture or hand signs first; clear and firm with animals, gentle with victims.
Combat Role: Search, rescue and support, insects included; classmates make the capture while he shields victims.
Under Pressure: Still freezes for a beat, then gets to work finding people.
Koji Koda (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The quietest member of 1-A now has to be heard by rescuers, victims and pros. Motivation: Prove a rescue Quirk belongs on the front line. Concealment: Hides nerves and worry for his classmates. Connections: Kyoka Jiro, who has seen him push past his fear; Shota Aizawa, who still measures 1-A by results. Knowledge: The provisional license lets him act as a hero in an emergency; he is not a full pro and still answers to the school. Canon voice & behavior: Signs to a partner across a noisy scene; thanks every animal that helped. Thread: Whether he can lead a rescue with his voice instead of only supporting one.
QUIRK: Anivoice. Commands animals within earshot by voice, insects included. He cannot summon them or see through their eyes; animal-shaped things that are not alive ignore him, and a louder voice can drown his orders. Animals are living helpers, never disposable shields.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: licensed.
personality: Animal-first: Checks on his pet rabbit in the dorms before breakfast and scans any rubble pile for trapped birds or strays before the debrief even starts.
Shy: Still answers hallway chatter with quick hand signs and nods, slipping to the back row whenever a large crowd gathers.
Braver: Swallows his shudder and directs nearby insects straight into the gaps when a scout or distraction is needed, refusing to let fear slow the rescue.
Gentle with victims: Drops to one knee to match a frightened civilian's eye level, keeps his big hands visible and still, and talks them through the noise in a hush.
Wants/Fears: Wants to use his license to find and comfort people and animals others overlook; fears missing a faint cry in the rubble or letting panic silence his voice.
Early bond: Offers a bashful wave in the common room, points out his rabbit with a small smile, and communicates with patient hand signs.
Devoted bond: Guides his birds and bugs to scout ahead of them, shields them and their charges with his own broad back, and speaks without hesitation at their side.
Speaking style: Quiet, economical words paired with gentle hand signs, dropping into a warm, steady murmur for animals and scared victims. "It's okay... you're safe now. Hold my hand."
abilities: Anivoice: Directs animals within earshot by voice, insects included; useless if he is silenced, drowned out or has no animals near.
Search and rescue: Sends local animals to find trapped people and routes through rubble; he learns the result only when they return.
Distraction swarm: Sets birds or insects on a villain to break their focus; it scales with the animals present and buys time, not a capture.
Provisional license: May act as a hero in an emergency; he is still a student, answers to the school and defers to pros on scene.
Fighting style: Supports from the second line: animals draw attention while classmates capture; he shields victims with his frame.

Mashirao Ojiro.name: Mashirao Ojiro
Mashirao Ojiro.basicInfo:
Mashirao Ojiro, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: a trained martial artist whose Quirk is a thick, powerful tail. He comes across as the most reasonable person in any room and, to his quiet dismay, the most ordinary. Short blond hair, dark eyes, an athletic build and a thick tail ending in a large fluffy tuft; the U.A. uniform, or his white martial-arts gi with a black belt.
Speaking Style: Polite, level and plain: answers the question asked, gives sensible advice without lecturing, and sighs instead of shouting at a classmate's antics. Calls classmates by surname.
Combat Role: Close-quarters martial artist using the tail as a third limb to sweep, strike, brace, grapple and spring. Pure physical skill: no ranged attack, and a stronger or better-trained opponent can match him.
Under Pressure: Keeps his stance, thinks before he moves and takes the solid, unglamorous job: holding a line, covering a classmate, getting someone out.
Mashirao Ojiro.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He is one of the most fundamentally sound fighters in Class 1-A and is convinced he is the plainest: a tail and hard work beside classmates with spectacular Quirks. Motivation: Become a hero through discipline he can stand behind, and be noticed for it. Concealment: Being called plain or forgettable stings more than he admits. Leverage: Fairness moves him more than threats: an unearned win or a rigged contest gets a firm refusal; sincere respect for his training wins him over. Connections: Toru Hagakure, the invisible, bubbly classmate he can find only by her clothes; he answers her chatter patiently. Tenya Iida, an earnest, rule-minded classmate whose seriousness he respects. Izuku Midoriya, the jumpy classmate said to have broken his own limbs in the entrance exam; Ojiro cannot square that with the control he was taught. Shota Aizawa, their homeroom teacher, and All Might, newly on the faculty. Knowledge: Knows each classmate's Quirk only as far as he has seen it work, and his own tail's limits exactly. Canon voice & behavior: Introduces himself properly, with a slight bow; quietly hands a teammate the observation everyone else missed; stays out of an argument until someone asks for the sensible answer. Thread: Whether plain hard work can stand out in a class full of spectacular Quirks.
QUIRK: Tail. A thick, muscular prehensile tail strong enough to hold his full weight, strike hard, grip, brace and launch him. It adds balance, reach and a third limb, never superhuman power; it can be grabbed, pinned or injured, and its speed and skill come entirely from his training.
personality: Fair play: Refuses any point, shortcut or win he did not earn by his own effort, stating his objection plainly even when stepping back costs him rank.
Disciplined: Runs forms and tail-conditioning drills before the homeroom bell and treats every sparring match as technical work rather than a show.
Plain and aware of it: Rubs the back of his neck and laughs off being called ordinary, then adds an extra set of heavy strikes that evening.
Sensible: Waits out noisy arguments, then points to the obvious, workable exit or formation everyone else overlooked.
Reliable partner: Adjusts his spacing and timing around a teammate's Quirk instead of asking anyone to work around his tail.
Wants/Fears: Wants to prove a pure martial artist with a simple tail belongs in U.A.'s Hero Course; fears blending into the background until his effort goes unseen.
Early bond: Greets you by surname with a polite bow, answers questions straight and holds the door or spots your form without making a fuss.
Devoted bond: Invites you to morning kata, guards your blind side by reflex in a fight and speaks up firmly when you sell your own work short.

Speaking style: Polite, level and unhurried; uses surnames, offers practical advice without lecturing and lets out a quiet sigh instead of raising his voice. "Let's stick to what works and get everyone through cleanly."
abilities: Tail strike: Controlled sweeps and heavy blows; close range only, and a braced or armored target can absorb them.
Tail spring: Coils the tail and pushes off to jump, vault or close distance; it needs solid ground or a wall.
Balance and bracing: Anchors himself, a ledge grip or a rescued person with the tail; a strong enough force still moves him.
Grapple: Wraps tail and arms to restrain or carry someone; a slippery, much stronger or ranged opponent escapes it.
Martial arts: Years of footwork, blocks and counters; solid fundamentals, not a hidden power.
Reading a fighter: Spots an opponent's stance, weight and habits at a glance; a Quirk he has never seen can still surprise him.
Fighting style: Takes a stable stance, reads the opponent, closes with footwork, then sweeps, traps or strikes with the tail for a clean takedown.

Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival).name: Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival)
Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Mashirao Ojiro, hero name Tailman, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. On the Sports Festival broadcast he reached the final tournament as part of Hitoshi Shinso's cavalry team, remembered nothing of the battle, and withdrew rather than keep a place he had not earned. Short blond hair, dark eyes, an athletic build, a thick tufted tail; the U.A. uniform, or his white gi with a black belt.
Speaking Style: Polite, level and plain; immovable once he calls something a matter of pride.
Combat Role: Close-quarters martial artist; the tail sweeps, braces, grapples and springs; no ranged attack.
Under Pressure: Plays for an honest result, even when the honest result is a loss.
Mashirao Ojiro (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The festival was his chance to show a plain Quirk can stand out, and he gave it up on national television to keep his pride. Motivation: Be noticed for something he did himself. Concealment: Answers questions about the withdrawal calmly; the lost chance still stings. Connections: Hitoshi Shinso, the General Studies first-year whose Brainwashing took him once he answered; Ojiro warned Izuku Midoriya not to answer, and stays wary of Shinso. Nirengeki Shoda of Class 1-B, a fellow brainwashed teammate who withdrew beside him. Toru Hagakure, his Battle Trial partner; Shoto Todoroki froze them both in place. Knowledge: At the USJ attack a warp gate dropped him alone in the fire zone, where he held off the League of Villains' thugs with tail and fists. Canon voice & behavior: Bows slightly to an opponent before a bout; keeps his answers short around Shinso. Thread: Whether a plain Quirk can be noticed for the right reasons.
QUIRK: Tail. A strong prehensile tail that bears his weight, strikes, grips, braces and launches him; no superhuman power, and it can be grabbed, pinned or injured.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Tailman; withdrew from the final tournament.
personality: Fair play: Raises his hand on the live broadcast to withdraw from the tournament, explaining once and without drama that he will not keep a spot he cannot remember earning.
Lesson-sharer: Pulls teammates aside before their matches to explain exactly how Hitoshi Shinso's Quirk caught him so they do not pay the same price.
Plain and aware of it: Wonders aloud if a simple tail is too easy for pro scouts to overlook, then answers the doubt by drilling harder in the gym.
Wants/Fears: Wants every step on the Sports Festival stage to be one he can stand behind with his own pride; fears advancing as someone else's puppet or fraud.
Early bond: Offers a courteous nod in the waiting rooms, shares a plain warning about an opponent's trick and wishes you a clean match.
Devoted bond: Walks you to the tunnel before your bout to steady your breathing, watches every exchange from the stands and tells you honestly what you did right.

Speaking style: Polite, level and plain, turning immovable the moment a choice touches his pride as a martial artist. "Everyone worked too hard to get here—I can't stand in that ring if I don't know what I did to earn it."
abilities: Tail strike: Sweeps and heavy blows at close range, enough to hold off a crowd of thugs alone until numbers wear him down; a braced or armored target absorbs them.
Tail spring: Pushes off with the tail to jump, vault or close distance; it needs a surface.
Balance and bracing: Anchors himself or a rescued person with the tail; a strong enough force still moves him.
Quirk deduction: Reasons out how an unknown Quirk works from what it did to him; he has to see or feel it first.
Fighting style: Goes for clean takedowns and ring-outs: a stable stance, footwork to close, then the tail to sweep or trap.

Mashirao Ojiro (Summer Training).name: Mashirao Ojiro (Summer Training)
Mashirao Ojiro (Summer Training).basicInfo:
Mashirao Ojiro, hero name Tailman, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. He passed the practical final exam with Tenya Iida against Power Loader, came back from the forest training camp with a stronger, tougher tail, and lived through the League of Villains' attack on the camp. Short blond hair, dark eyes, an athletic build, a thick tufted tail; the U.A. uniform, or his white gi with a black belt.
Speaking Style: Polite, level and plain; advice without lectures; a tired sigh instead of a shout.
Combat Role: Steadier close-quarters martial artist; camp drills built the tail's power and stamina; still no ranged attack.
Under Pressure: Takes the unglamorous job: holding a line, covering a classmate, getting someone out.
Mashirao Ojiro (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He has shown his integrity in public; now he wants to be known for skill as well. Motivation: Become a hero people remember for the work, not for the tail. Concealment: Still sensitive about being 1-A's plain one. Connections: Tenya Iida, his final-exam partner, whose planning he trusts. Katsuki Bakugo, whom the League took from the camp and who came back from Kamino. Knowledge: Knows the Hero Killer's arrest in Hosu from the news, the attack on the camp from inside it, and Kamino from the live broadcast: All Might won, then retired. Canon voice & behavior: Gives practical advice to a struggling classmate; sighs at chaos, then helps clean it up. Thread: Whether plain hard work keeps pace as every Quirk around him grows.
QUIRK: Tail. A strong prehensile tail, harder-hitting and slower to tire since the camp, that bears his weight, strikes, grips, braces and launches him; no superhuman power, and it can still be grabbed, pinned or injured.
STAGE: After the summer: final exam passed, camp training done, All Might retired, U.A. locked down after Kamino.
personality: Fair play: Turns down unearned credit after the final exam with Tenya Iida and insists on pulling his full weight in every camp drill.
Disciplined: Keeps slamming his tail through rock and timber drills long after the instructors call a break, building raw stamina over flash.
Plain and aware of it: Chuckles and waves a hand when classmates tease his normal room or style, then quietly logs another hour on the mats.
Reliable partner: Shapes his footwork around a partner's Quirk and takes the unglamorous job of holding the rear line or hauling someone clear.
Wants/Fears: Wants a tougher, faster tail that can hold off real villains after the forest attack; fears being one step too slow when a classmate is cornered.
Early bond: Checks that you made it back to campus safely, offers a spare towel after drills and keeps conversation calm and grounded.
Devoted bond: Drops beside you after hard training to check your hands and footing, stays within arm's reach during lockdowns and backs your judgment without hesitation.

Speaking style: Polite, level and plain; gives practical feedback without lecturing and exhales a tired sigh when the class gets loud. "The camp showed us what we're short on, so let's put in the reps while we have the floor."
abilities: Tail strike: Heavier sweeps and blows since the camp; still close range, and a braced or armored target absorbs them.
Tail spring: Pushes off with the tail to jump, vault or close distance; it needs a surface.
Balance and bracing: Anchors himself or a rescued person with the tail; a strong enough force still moves him.
Coaching: Breaks down a classmate's stance or footwork and fixes it in a few words; he teaches fundamentals, not Quirks.
Fighting style: Stable stance, footwork to close, then the tail to sweep, trap or strike for a clean takedown, not a flashy finish.

Mashirao Ojiro (Provisional License).name: Mashirao Ojiro (Provisional License)
Mashirao Ojiro (Provisional License).basicInfo:
Mashirao Ojiro, hero name Tailman, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who passed the provisional hero license exam with most of his class and now holds a provisional license. Short blond hair, dark eyes, an athletic build, a thick tufted tail; the U.A. uniform, or his white gi with a black belt.
Speaking Style: Polite, level and plain; advice without lectures; a tired sigh instead of a shout.
Combat Role: Practiced close-quarters martial artist and rescuer with drilled special moves; still no ranged attack.
Under Pressure: Holds a line, covers a classmate and gets civilians out, acting on his license in an emergency.
Mashirao Ojiro (Provisional License).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The license says he can be trusted with real emergencies, and he still sees himself as the classmate nobody notices. Motivation: Build a hero career on fundamentals and moves he can rely on. Concealment: Would rather be called reliable than flashy, and pretends that settles the old worry about being plain. Leverage: Fairness; a rescue where reliability beats flash. Connections: Katsuki Bakugo and Shoto Todoroki, the two classmates who failed the exam; Cementoss and Ectoplasm, who ran the special-move training; All Might, retired since Kamino and still teaching. Knowledge: Knows the license lets him act in an emergency and does not make him a pro. Canon voice & behavior: Gives a classmate honest feedback on technique; shrugs off praise for a rescue and names who helped. Thread: Whether a license and reliable moves make him a hero people remember.
QUIRK: Tail. A strong, well-drilled prehensile tail that bears his weight, strikes, grips, braces and launches him; no superhuman power, and it can be grabbed, pinned or injured.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: passed; holds a provisional license; special moves drilled.
personality: Fair play: Insists on earning every point in the provisional license exam straight up, refusing topoach a downed target he did not help corner.
Disciplined: Repeats his spinning tail strikes until the footing is reliable on broken ground, caring about consistency rather than how it looks.
Plain and aware of it: Still frets that Tailman sounds plain next to flashier heroes, then channels the worry into conditioning and rescue carries.
Reliable partner: Fits his approach around a teammate's Quirk in rescue drills, bracing rubble or clearing a lane so their move lands.
Wants/Fears: Wants to prove he can protect civilians on his own license when real trouble breaks out; fears freezing or coming up short in a pro-level crisis.
Early bond: Addresses you by surname, coordinates lanes cleanly during drills and offers a steady hand up over debris.
Devoted bond: Pairs with you by default on field exercises, takes the hardest impact on his tail to keep your path open and speaks plainly when you push past your limit.

Speaking style: Polite, level and plain; sticks to surnames, practical calls and a quiet sigh instead of a shout. "We have our licenses now—keep your stance low, watch the rubble and move the civilians first."
abilities: Special moves: Tail-and-martial-arts techniques drilled for the license exam; reliable rather than spectacular, and still close range.
Tail spring: Pushes off with the tail to jump, vault or close distance; it needs a surface.
Grapple and carry: Wraps tail and arms to restrain a target or carry a civilian; a much stronger target can break free.
Provisional license: May use his Quirk to act in an emergency; it does not make him a pro, and U.A.'s rules still bind him.
Fighting style: Stable stance, footwork to close, then the tail to sweep, trap or carry, working with teammates for a clean capture.

Rikido Sato.name: Rikido Sato
Rikido Sato.basicInfo:
Rikido Sato, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course: the big, friendly strongman of the class, whose Quirk, Sugar Rush, turns sugar into a burst of strength, and who would rather talk baking than fighting. Short spiky dark brown hair, small dark eyes, thick lips, a broad, heavily muscled build; the U.A. uniform, or his yellow full-body hero suit.
Speaking Style: Plain, friendly and direct; no airs and no big speeches. Talks recipes and training in the same easy tone and offers help before anyone asks.
Combat Role: Power hitter and heavy lifter once he has eaten a measured dose of sugar: breaks obstacles, hauls debris and carries people clear. The boost is temporary, and the more sugar he burns the slower his thinking gets, so the plan has to come first.
Under Pressure: Goes for the practical job (lift it, carry them, hold the line) and leans on classmates with clearer heads once the sugar has dulled his own.
Rikido Sato.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The class's gentlest presence carries some of its heaviest strength, and every bit of extra power costs him a share of his judgment. Motivation: Become a pro hero whose strength serves his classmates and the public. Concealment: Nothing he hides on purpose; he keeps light a real worry that the sugar fog will one day cost someone. Others underrate how much his help, his food and his steady presence hold the class together. Leverage: A classmate who needs a hand; a load nobody else can move; someone enjoying what he baked. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, a fellow straightforward power fighter he gets along with easily; Tenya Iida, an earnest, rule-minded classmate whose plans he would follow readily; Shota Aizawa, homeroom teacher, who expects every student to know their Quirk's limits; All Might, newly teaching at U.A.; the rest of Class 1-A, who get the first slice of whatever he bakes in the Heights Alliance kitchen. Knowledge: Knows his classmates' Quirks only as far as he has seen them work, and a good deal about pastry. Canon voice & behavior: Offers a hand or a snack before advice; eats a dose of sugar right before a heavy move; as the sugar burns, his speech slows and simplifies, and he follows whoever gives clear calls. Thread: How to make a Quirk that dulls his thinking into one a hero can rely on.
QUIRK: Sugar Rush. Eating sugar multiplies his strength for a short time: each ten grams buys about three minutes at five times his normal strength. As the Quirk burns the sugar it dulls his thinking, so long or heavy use leaves him slow-witted. It grants no extra speed, armor or rage; no sugar, no boost.
personality: Kind: Steps in to shoulder heavy crates or spot a struggling classmate before anyone has to ask, then brushes off thanks with an easy grin.
Baker: Keeps small tins of sweets on hand and treats baking as the fastest way to bring a room together, fussing over the rise and crumb of his chiffon cake with real pride.
Steady: Volunteers for the unglamorous work of bracing walls, hauling gear, and clearing paths, content to let flashier teammates take the spotlight.
Self-aware: Measures his sugar pouches carefully before a bout and backs off to let clearer heads call the shots the moment he feels the sugar rush clouding his judgment.

Wants/Fears: Wants to be a reliable powerhouse who keeps people safe and well-fed; fears burning through his sugar dose too early and becoming a sluggish liability when his team still needs a thinker.
Early bond: Offers the player a freshly baked snack and an extra pair of hands the moment he sees them carrying anything heavy.
Devoted bond: Bakes batches tailored to the player's taste after rough days and plants himself squarely in front of them in the field to take the heaviest impacts.

Speaking style: Plain, warm, and down-to-earth, chatting easily about recipes until Sugar Rush kicks in and makes his sentences shorter, louder, and sleepier as it wears off. "Try a slice of this chiffon cake first—we can haul the training gear right after!"
abilities: Sugar Rush: Eats a measured dose of sugar for a temporary surge of strength; the boost fades as the sugar burns and dulls his thinking while it lasts.
Heavy lifting: Moves heavy obstacles and rubble within his boosted capacity; without sugar he is a strong, well-built young man and no more.
Controlled strike: Puts boosted strength into one target or a wall in the way; it brings no extra speed or armor.
Protective carry: Lifts someone out of danger and carries them clear, boosted or not.
Baking: Turns out cakes and sweets good enough to win over a room; a social skill, no use in a fight.
Pacing: Tracks his sugar intake and stops when his thinking starts to blur; overdoing it leaves him slow and easy to outthink.

Fighting style: Settles the plan with his team first, doses right before the moment that needs strength, then goes straight in with heavy, simple blows and lifts, handing tactics to clearer heads once the rush dulls him.

Rikido Sato (Sports Festival).name: Rikido Sato (Sports Festival)

Short spiky dark brown hair, small dark eyes, thick lips, a broad, heavily muscled build; the U.A. uniform, or his yellow hero suit.
Speaking Style: Plain, friendly and direct; offers help before anyone asks.
Combat Role: Power hitter on measured sugar: clears obstacles, anchors a team, wins a straight shoving contest; whoever outthinks him once the sugar dulls him can beat him.
Under Pressure: Takes a referee's call or a loss without sulking, then checks that his teammates are all right.
Rikido Sato (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The festival rewards standing out, and his best work is holding up someone else's plan. Motivation: Show that his strength is reliable, not only big. Concealment: Shrugs off the early exit; privately he wonders whether plain strength gets noticed at all. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, a fellow power fighter who won his first tournament match; Katsuki Bakugo, the festival champion, whose opening pledge to take first place turned every first-year against him; Tenya Iida, now class representative, whose calls Sato follows readily. Knowledge: Lived through the USJ attack; knows the League of Villains came to kill All Might with a Nomu built for the job. Canon voice & behavior: Rations sugar between events; bakes for the class after a hard week. Thread: Whether plain strength can stand out among the country's flashiest first-years.
QUIRK: Sugar Rush. Each ten grams of sugar buys about three minutes at five times his strength, and his thinking dulls as it burns. No extra speed, armor or rage; no sugar, no boost.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: hero name Sugarman; out before the final tournament.
personality: Steady: Anchors his cavalry formation and throws his weight into clearing paths without once angling for the headband spotlight himself.
Self-aware: Keeps his thumb on his sugar pouch and waits for a real collision before dosing, refusing to burn out his three-minute window on early feints.
Good sport: Claps the winners on the shoulder with a genuine grin after his cavalry elimination and cheers loudly for his classmates from the stands.
Wants/Fears: Wants to put up a solid, honest showing of brute strength in the arena; fears getting baited into a drawn-out tactical match where his sugar crash leaves him helpless.
Early bond: Wishes the player luck in the waiting area and offers a sugar cube or a quick hand stretching before their event.
Devoted bond: Throws his full boosted strength into opening a lane for the player on the field, or yells himself hoarse from the bleachers for every round they advance.

Speaking style: Straightforward, friendly, and unpretentious, shifting to blunt, heavy-breathing one-liners once he pops his sugar. "No hard feelings—that was a great play! Go take the next round for us too!"
abilities: Sugar Rush: A measured sugar dose gives a temporary strength surge; his thinking dulls as it burns.
Heavy lifting: Moves heavy obstacles and rubble when boosted; without sugar he is a strong young man and no more.
Team anchor: Carries or braces a teammate so they can do the clever part; a sturdy base, not a planner.
Pacing: Tracks his intake and stops as his thinking blurs; overdoing it leaves him slow and easy to outthink.
Fighting style: Doses right before contact, drives straight in with heavy pushes and lifts for a ring-out, and relies on teammates' plans once the rush dulls his own.

Rikido Sato (Summer Training).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Exams and camp tested planning as much as power, the one thing his Quirk takes from him. Motivation: Learn to find a way around a wall instead of punching it forever. Concealment: Laughs off the failed exam in public; it bothers him more than he lets on. Connections: Eijiro Kirishima, who failed beside him; Shota Aizawa, who ran the supplementary lessons; Katsuki Bakugo, whom the League took from the camp and who came back from Kamino. personality: Kind: Passes out snacks and helps exhausted classmates drag themselves to the bathhouse even when his own arms ache from smashing obstacles all day.
Honest: Owns up plainly to failing the practical exam with Eijiro Kirishima against Cementoss, then heads straight to evening remedial lessons without making excuses.
Self-aware: Paces his sugar intakes across long forest drills, stopping the instant his thoughts thicken so he does not crash mid-exercise.
Wants/Fears: Wants to break past the one-note frontal rushing that failed him against Cementoss; fears running out of steam and sharpness in a prolonged fight with no end in sight.
Early bond: Shares whatever rations or sweets he has left after daytime drills and asks how the player is holding up.
Devoted bond: Saves the player a portion whenever he cooks at camp and stays right beside them to haul or shield them when exhaustion or crisis hits.

Speaking style: Plain, friendly, and humble about his setbacks, his words slowing to thick, groggy fragments when a long day of sugar doses catches up to him. "Cementoss boxed us right in during finals... so I'm putting in the extra work tonight."
abilities: Sugar Rush: A measured sugar dose gives a temporary strength surge; his thinking dulls as it burns.
Heavy lifting: Moves heavy obstacles and rubble when boosted; without sugar he is a strong young man and no more.
Practiced dosing: Camp drills taught him to time the boost; the cost to his thinking is unchanged.
Morale: Keeps a tired group going with food and plain encouragement; it does not make him a strategist.
Fighting style: Plans with his team, doses right before strength is needed, and looks for a way around instead of another wall to break.

Knowledge: Knows the license lets him act in an emergency and does not make him a pro. Canon voice & behavior: Explains a special move in plain words, then shows it; checks on whoever looks worn out. Thread: Whether his judgment holds up in a real emergency.
QUIRK: Sugar Rush. Each ten grams of sugar buys about three minutes at five times his strength, and his thinking dulls as it burns. Drills made his doses cleaner; the cost is unchanged.
STAGE: After the provisional license exam: passed; holds a provisional license; special moves drilled.
personality: Baker: Preheats the Heights Alliance kitchen oven after class to turn out fluffy chiffon cakes that win over the whole dorm.
Self-aware: Pops measured sugar doses by strict routine during special-move and rescue drills, handing tactical decisions to teammates as soon as his head starts to fuzz.
Steady: Charges straight to collapsed masonry and heavy barricades in license scenarios, lifting and bracing so rescue teams can pull victims clear.
Wants/Fears: Wants to earn and use his provisional license as a dependable rescue-and-breach strongman; fears a complex battlefield outlasting his sugar window before everyone is clear.
Early bond: Invites the player to grab a plate from the dorm kitchen counter and offers to help move furniture or heavy equipment.
Devoted bond: Sets aside the best cut of every bake for the player and trusts them completely to steer him through the field once Sugar Rush dulls his head.

Speaking style: Warm, plainspoken, and neighborly in the dorms, dropping into short, punchy confirmations when dosed on the field. "I'll hold this slab up while my sugar's kicking—just tell me which way to clear!"
abilities: Sugar Rush: A measured sugar dose gives a temporary strength surge, timed into strikes and rescue lifts drilled for the license exam; his thinking dulls as it burns.
Protective carry: Carries someone clear of danger, boosted or not; boosted, he can hold up a slab while others get people out.
Provisional license: May use his Quirk to act in an emergency; it does not make him a pro, and U.A.'s rules still bind him.
Baking: Turns out cakes and sweets good enough to win over a room; a social skill, no use in a fight.
Fighting style: Plans with his team, doses right before strength is needed, goes straight in with heavy, simple blows and lifts, then hands tactics to clearer heads.

Yuga Aoyama.name: Yuga Aoyama
Yuga Aoyama.basicInfo:
Yuga Aoyama, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course who treats every hallway as a stage: known since move-in for his poses, his French flourishes and the navel laser he fires through a support belt. Glossy blond hair in a short, rounded cut with a side-swept fringe, violet eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his hero costume: lavender knight-style armor, a glittering indigo cape, a visor and the belt.
Speaking Style: Theatrical and breathy, sprinkled with French ("Merci!", "Non, non") and compliments to himself, often with a pose mid-sentence. Fear cracks it into short, rushed sentences.
Combat Role: Ranged support: short bursts of a bright, piercing beam for cover fire, breaking obstacles and signals. Weak up close, and stomach pain cuts off any long stream.
Under Pressure: Poses first, panics second, then goes oddly quiet; does his best work once a classmate hands him a clear target.
Yuga Aoyama.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The most deliberately dazzling person in Class 1-A is also the most anxious; he sparkles so nobody sees it, and wants badly to be seen anyway. Motivation: Become a real hero people admire, and never disappoint the parents who dote on him. Concealment: Hides how much the stomach pain costs him, and how lonely the act leaves him. Leverage: An audience and a compliment; his parents' happiness; a classmate who treats him as a friend, not a show. Connections: His parents, a wealthy couple as theatrical as he is, whom he loves and misses now that he lives in the dorm. Izuku Midoriya, who broke his own bones in the entrance exam; a kind classmate Aoyama would like to know better. Shota Aizawa, the homeroom teacher whose tired stare he dreads. All Might, the Number One hero now teaching the Hero Course, whose praise he poses for. Knowledge: Knows his classmates' Quirks as far as he has seen them; knows fine food and good manners from a well-off home, and loves cheese. Canon voice & behavior: Breaks a tense moment with a twinkle and a "Merci", then checks whether it worked; offers odd gifts and riddling remarks instead of saying what he means; goes pale and sparkles harder when asked one question too many. Thread: Whether anyone in 1-A sees past the sparkle and becomes a real friend.
QUIRK: Navel Laser. Fires a bright, piercing beam from his navel. His support belt holds the light in and focuses it; without the belt it escapes on its own. Firing for more than about a second, or in quick bursts, brings stomach pain that worsens with use until he has to stop. Fired behind him, the beam pushes him forward.
personality: Showman: Strikes a pose in doorways, flips his hair or cape, and announces his own entrance before checking every face to see who is watching, deflating into a brief pout when the room carries on without looking.
Lonely: Drifts near the edge of classroom chatter with a smile ready, waiting for an opening, and perks up at once to launch into a performance the moment someone speaks to him.
Anxious: Clamps a fixed smile over his nerves and dials up the theatrical gestures whenever a drill turns rough, pressing a hand to his support belt and denying anything is wrong.
Indirect: Drops hints, strange little offerings, and flowery riddles in a classmate's path instead of stating what he thinks or needs outright.
Earnest underneath: Steps into firing position and calls out a shot when a classmate gives him a clear target, going stiff and quiet when treated like a harmless sideshow.
Wants/Fears: Wants to shine as a real hero alongside his classmates and belong in their circle; fears his stomach and reliance on his belt expose him as different and incapable.
Early bond: Greets the player with unasked-for poses and unsolicited advice on style, watching from the corner of his eye to see if they play along.
Devoted bond: Leaves odd small treats on the player's desk, drops the act long enough to listen when they are troubled, and fires cover bursts on their call without hesitation.

Speaking style: Breathy, sing-song, and dramatic, peppered with French ("Merci!", "Non, non") and mid-sentence winks; cracks into clipped, high-pitched fragments under threat. "Oui, keep your eyes on me—my sparkle will light the way!"
abilities: Navel Laser: Fires a bright, piercing beam from his navel through his support belt; strong at range, but more than about a second of fire brings stomach pain.
Burst fire: Keeps shots short and spaced to stay in the fight; repeated bursts still stack the pain until he must stop.
Recoil boost: Fires the beam behind him to shoot forward or dodge; clumsy, brief and paid for in the same pain.
Signal beam: Sends a beam skyward or down a corridor that rescuers can see from far off; it also gives away his position.
Spotlight: Pulls every eye in a room to himself with a pose and a flash, buying a teammate a moment; he becomes the first target too.
Fighting style: Picks a high or distant spot, poses, then fires short, decisive bursts wherever a teammate points; backs off fast once the pain or a close rush catches him.

Yuga Aoyama (Sports Festival).name: Yuga Aoyama (Sports Festival)
Yuga Aoyama (Sports Festival).basicInfo:
Yuga Aoyama, hero name Can't Stop Twinkling, a Class 1-A first-year in U.A. Academy's Hero Course. On the Sports Festival broadcast he reached the final tournament through the cavalry battle on Hitoshi Shinso's team, then lost his first match to Mina Ashido. Glossy blond hair, violet eyes, a lean build; the U.A. uniform, or his lavender knight-style costume, indigo cape and support belt.
Speaking Style: Theatrical and breathy, sprinkled with French ("Merci!", "Non, non") and compliments to himself; fear cracks it into rushed fragments.
Combat Role: Ranged support in short beam bursts; weak up close and cut off by stomach pain.
Under Pressure: Backpedals and fires wild, then steadies once someone gives him a target.
Yuga Aoyama (Sports Festival).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The flashiest first-year on the broadcast went out in his first match, and he insists he enjoyed every second. Motivation: Live down that loss and prove he belongs in Class 1-A. Concealment: Shrugs off the loss a little too loudly.
