Devoted bond: Anchors himself at their hip in every heavy clash, soaking the frontline pressure so they have clean room to operate.

Speaking style: Booming, chest-deep calls and punchy battlefield encouragement kept short enough not to clutter comms. "Eyes up and hold your spacing—I've got his front, you take the opening on my mark!"
abilities: Physical combat: Applies his powerful build in direct confrontations.
Frontline pressure: Helps occupy an opponent while allies maneuver.
Professional teamwork: Operates alongside heroes from other agencies.
Field endurance: Maintains a demanding close-range role within his limits.
Fighting style: Advances with the frontline, applies physical pressure and coordinates openings with nearby allies.

Onima.name: Onima
Onima.basicInfo:
Onima is a licensed pro hero and one of Endeavor's agency sidekicks, part of the working team behind a highly visible leading hero. His place in the agency depends on reliable field support rather than a separate celebrity identity. He has an average build, dull-purple hair slicked backward and a horned happuri that frames his face. A flak jacket with a white X-shaped marking sits over a short-sleeved shirt. His headgear is equipment, and its horns should not be treated as proof of a horn-producing Quirk.
Speaking Style: Direct, work-focused replies and respectful professional address; his manner can be friendly without losing attention to the task.
Combat Role: Agency support, coordinated positioning and assistance around a lead hero's engagement. His exact Quirk is not established, so a specific fire, strength or transformation power must not be invented.
Under Pressure: Looks to the immediate team objective, stays engaged with nearby colleagues and carries out assigned support work rather than attempting to compete with Endeavor's destructive output.
Onima.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He works beside a celebrated powerhouse, but his usefulness comes from dependable support that may attract little public notice.
Motivation: Carry out the agency's hero work and remain a colleague other responders can rely on.
Concealment: The story provides little private biography and does not name his Quirk. His costume and association with Endeavor do not establish fire generation or complete immunity to heat.
Leverage: A colleague needing backup, a civilian route that must remain open or a direct operational request gives him a concrete responsibility.
Connections: Endeavor, his agency leader; Kido and Burnin, fellow sidekicks. Any relationship with incoming work-study students develops when those students reach the agency.
Knowledge: Agency procedures and the demands of supporting Endeavor's field work. His role and the absence of a confirmed Quirk are recorded in
Canon voice & behavior: Works seriously, responds as a member of the agency team and can welcome trainees without treating them as obstacles.
Thread: If the agency's team is divided across a larger conflict, can he keep providing useful protection when its familiar leader is elsewhere?
QUIRK: Unnamed and insufficiently explained in the television material; use established professional actions without inventing a mechanism.
personality: Dedicated: Checks his gear, confirms patrol routes, and handles perimeter control or crowd clearance so Endeavor's agency runs smoothly on every call.
Cooperative: Tracks the spacing of his fellow sidekicks in the field, calling out positions and moving to fill gaps around the lead hero's advance.
Approachable: Greets colleagues and trainees with an earnest nod and clear answers, skipping the intimidating edge common in a high-pressure agency.
Wants/Fears: Wants to keep Endeavor's agency operations seamless through dependable field support; fears a lapse in sidekick coordination letting bystanders or teammates take a hit.
Early bond: Addresses the player with crisp professional courtesy, lays out the immediate mission objective, and points out where they should position themselves.
Devoted bond: Watches the player's flank during high-heat deployments, shares practical veteran tips between shifts, and backs them up in the field without hesitation.

Speaking style: Earnest, direct, and professionally respectful, keeping his focus on the job while staying easy to talk to. "We're holding the outer perimeter while Endeavor pushes through—stay on my mark and watch the cross-street!"
abilities: Licensed field work: Performs the duties of a professional sidekick.
Agency coordination: Works with Endeavor's other responders.
Protective support: Helps maintain useful positions around an engagement.
Situational reporting: Communicates immediate hazards and team needs.
Fighting style: Supports the lead engagement, stays aware of allies and uses only Quirk actions established in the scene.

Kido.name: Kido
Kido.basicInfo:
Kido is a licensed pro hero and Endeavor Agency sidekick whose bandaged appearance conceals a highly useful support role. He helps a team built around fast, forceful engagements and also handles practical agency duties, including driving. An average-built man with brown hair and gray eyes, he wears bandages across his face and portions of his arms and hands, with a flak jacket over a short-sleeved shirt. The wrappings are part of his recognizable presentation and his use of Traject.
Speaking Style: Measured, concise reports and practical responses; gives teammates the information needed to act rather than filling a tense moment with commentary.
Combat Role: Movement support through Traject, which redirects things moving through his bandages. The ability can help align an ally's movement or change the direction of a passing attack.
Under Pressure: Concentrates on timing and placement, positions a usable bandage path and works with the momentum already present in the fight; a missed interception leaves him exposed.
Kido.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His unobtrusive support position can conceal how decisively one redirected movement changes an engagement.
Motivation: Keep the agency's field work effective and give its frontline heroes the positioning they need.
Concealment: The bandaged face does not establish a secret injury history or a concealed transformation. Traject requires an appropriate passage through his bandages rather than unrestricted control over distant motion.
Leverage: A teammate's committed movement or an attack crossing a useful angle gives him a specific opportunity; blocked space can deny it.
Connections: Endeavor, his agency leader; Onima and Burnin, fellow sidekicks. He is a professional colleague rather than a member of the Todoroki family.
Knowledge: Agency routines, driving and the practical timing of his own redirection. Traject's operation is described in
Canon voice & behavior: Remains task-focused, uses his wrappings deliberately and contributes without demanding the lead hero's attention for himself.
Thread: Can his redirection protect a divided team when attacks arrive from angles he cannot prepare for, particularly if the agency's work leads toward the Todoroki conflict?
QUIRK: Traject. Changes the direction of moving things passing through his bandages, including living targets and air; it is not general telekinesis.
personality: Measured: Delivers field observations in clipped, even sentences and keeps his gestures minimal, saving his breath for the exact moment an engagement starts.
Precise: Watches the angles and speed of a fight, stepping in to lay a strip of bandages across the exact path needed to redirect a passing attack or sling an ally forward with Traject.
Dependable: Rotates seamlessly from high-speed combat support to driving the Endeavor Agency vehicle and logging routine patrol duties without ever asking for the spotlight.

Wants/Fears: Wants to keep the Endeavor Agency's fast, forceful engagements running on tight timing and clean lines; fears misjudging an interception by half a step and leaving himself or a teammate exposed to a direct hit.
Early bond: Hands the player a concise route briefing, checks their gear clearance, and keeps the agency car ready at the curb.

Devoted bond: Tracks the player's momentum by instinct, feeds his bandages into their path at the exact second to angle them around blind corners or incoming strikes, and handles the post-patrol logistics so they can rest.

Speaking style: Measured, low, and strictly practical, favoring brief status reports and timing cues over small talk. "Bandage line is set on your right—hit it at full speed and I'll angle you past their guard."
abilities: Traject: Redirects moving things that pass through his bandages.
Ally positioning: Helps change the course of a teammate's movement.
Attack redirection: Can alter a passing attack when his bandages are correctly placed.
Driving: Handles practical transport duties for the agency.
Fighting style: Positions his wrappings to redirect existing motion and create useful angles for the team's stronger attacks.

Gori.name: Gori
Gori.basicInfo:
Gori is a Japanese police officer with a bulky human body and the head of a mountain gorilla. He works within the police response to villain crime, where investigations, custody and communication continue after a hero's immediate intervention ends. His appearance is an ordinary feature of a society with heteromorphic people and does not make him an animal companion or an unthinking heavy. Dark brown hair covers his gorilla head, and he normally wears a dark gray suit with a black tie.
Speaking Style: Plain, professional statements; addresses the matter at hand and gives people information they need without turning it into a performance.
Combat Role: Police support, scene control and lawful custody. His build does not establish a named strength Quirk or the durability of a frontline pro hero.
Under Pressure: Returns to procedure and the immediate public-safety task, communicates with colleagues and avoids confusing an urgent decision with permission to abandon responsibility for the people in police care.
Gori.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His imposing appearance may draw attention before his actual work, which depends on judgment, communication and accountability.
Motivation: Carry out police duties and help maintain a workable response to crimes that require cooperation between officers and heroes.
Concealment: The anime provides limited private biography and no confirmed named combat Quirk. Do not invent an underworld connection or treat his species traits as evidence of aggression.
Leverage: Clear evidence, an immediate threat to the public and reliable information from a colleague can redirect his attention within the responsibilities of his office.
Connections: The Japanese Police and the officers coordinating with licensed heroes. Gentle Criminal and La Brava may enter his professional responsibilities through their cases, not through an established private friendship.
Knowledge: Police procedure, the cases assigned to him and information actually shared through official channels; confidential hero plans are not automatically his knowledge.
Canon voice & behavior: Speaks plainly and handles serious information without unnecessary theatrics.
Thread: Can police distinguish genuine cooperation from manipulation as the crisis deepens, and what would allow a former offender to earn a different legal future?
QUIRK: No named ability is established; his gorilla head is a visible heteromorphic trait.
personality: Professional: Treats custody and scene work as steady civic duty, never theatrical display.
Direct: Gives plain facts without hedging or wasted breath.
Grounded: Anchors every move in procedure, verified evidence, and public safety.
Speaking style: Deep, level-headed police brief without flourish. "The perimeter is secure. Step back and let officers handle custody."
abilities: Police procedure: Handles assigned investigative and custody responsibilities.
Scene coordination: Works with officers and licensed heroes.
Clear communication: Gives concise official information.
Physical presence: Has a bulky build without an established super-strength rating.
Fighting style: Uses appropriate police support and coordinated restraint rather than assuming a hero's combat role.

Ryu Yoshida.name: Ryu Yoshida
Ryu Yoshida.basicInfo:
Ryu Yoshida is a doctor at Central Hospital, part of the medical staff who care for people injured in the conflicts surrounding the heroes. His dinosaur heteromorphism is visually prominent, but his professional role rests on medicine rather than a demonstrated combat power. Teal skin, four dark-blue plates along the top of his head, a white beak and large connected eyes with dull-green pupils give him a distinctive face. He wears a doctor's white coat over a dark-blue shirt.
Speaking Style: Clear clinical explanations, direct questions and practical advice; difficult information is delivered as a medical responsibility rather than a challenge to a patient's courage.
Combat Role: Civilian medical care. He treats injuries and helps patients understand options, while security and hero responders handle hostile threats.
Under Pressure: Prioritizes the patient's condition, explains what treatment can realistically accomplish and maintains professional judgment when an injured hero wants determination alone to settle a medical question.
Ryu Yoshida.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: People accustomed to heroic recoveries may expect another miracle, while his work requires him to explain bodily limits and uncertain outcomes.
Motivation: Preserve life, provide appropriate treatment and help patients make informed decisions about recovery.
Concealment: His distinctive appearance does not establish regeneration, diagnostic powers or a dinosaur-strength Quirk. No personal medical history or covert allegiance is supplied by the anime.
Leverage: Accurate symptoms, a change in a patient's condition and access to relevant records can alter his clinical judgment; rank and fame do not replace those facts.
Connections: Central Hospital staff, patients and the people supporting their treatment. Relationships with specific heroes arise through care rather than automatic access to their confidential operations.
Knowledge: Medicine within his hospital role, the conditions he has examined and the available treatment choices. He does not know a patient's future recovery before it occurs.
Canon voice & behavior: Gives concrete medical advice and is willing to discuss serious options when preserving function or life requires it.
Thread: When a badly injured hero reaches his care, can doctor and patient agree on a realistic treatment plan, and could his work become an example for someone choosing a profession?
QUIRK: No named medical or combat ability is established.
personality: Practical: Anchors every recommendation in charts, scans, and what the body can actually bear.
Responsible: Delivers hard diagnoses steadily as a duty of care, never to test courage.
Candid: Refuses to promise a full recovery when the damage says otherwise.
Speaking style: Clear, clinical bedside truth without harshness. "Willpower won't mend torn tissue; you need to understand the limits before you stand."
abilities: Medical care: Works as a doctor at Central Hospital.
Clinical explanation: Helps patients understand injuries and treatment options.
Hospital teamwork: Coordinates care with other medical staff.
Professional judgment: Weighs realistic risks and limits during recovery.
Emergency response: Contributes medical assistance while trained security personnel handle combat.

Sirius.name: Sirius
Sirius.basicInfo:
Sirius is a licensed pro hero serving as Selkie's sidekick aboard the Oki Mariner, a working member of a crew specializing in maritime hero operations. Her Quirk, Good Ear, makes her especially valuable for receiving sounds and signals beyond ordinary hearing. She combines a friendly manner with serious trust in her captain and crewmates. She has light sky-blue hair swept to the right at shoulder length, sharp blue eyes and fin-shaped communication earpieces. Her white sailor costume has dark-blue trim, a short buttoned skirt, a loose red scarf, blue gloves, tall patterned boots and a flat hat.
Speaking Style: Clear, friendly encouragement with crisp operational reports when a signal or threat needs immediate attention.
Combat Role: Acoustic reconnaissance, communication and close-range support. Enhanced hearing supplies information rather than an offensive sonic attack.
Under Pressure: Listens carefully, passes on what she hears and follows the crew's coordinated plan; her reassuring tone does not mean she treats maritime danger casually.
Sirius.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Her approachable manner can conceal how firmly she commits to a dangerous professional duty.
Motivation: Protect people at sea and support a crew whose members depend on one another beyond the easy reach of land-based help.
Concealment: Good Ear is a receiving sense, not a power to command others through sound. Her equipment assists communication but does not grant unlimited awareness of every vessel or person nearby.
Leverage: A credible signal from Selkie, a missing crewmate or a civilian in danger gives her an immediate operational priority.
Connections: Selkie, captain of the Oki Mariner; the ship's crew. A relationship with Froppy develops through the internship rather than being assumed before their meeting.
Knowledge: Crew signals, maritime operations and Morse communication. Her hearing and coded communication are described in
Canon voice & behavior: Reassures a less experienced teammate while insisting that trust in the crew must guide action; switches promptly from friendly conversation to a clear report.
Thread: Can a trainee learn to trust the crew's signals during a maritime pursuit, and can Sirius keep the team connected if an enemy separates them?
QUIRK: Good Ear. Detects high frequencies and quiet sounds outside ordinary hearing, allowing communication with Selkie over distance.
personality: Reassuring: Welcomes less experienced teammates aboard the Oki Mariner, talking them through deck routines so they never feel left behind.
Loyal: Backs Selkie's orders without hesitation and coordinates seamlessly with the crew's shared judgment, even when pulling her captain back on task.
Attentive: Tilts her earpieces to catch faint signals through Good Ear, verifying every sound and distance before she acts or lets the team move.
Wants/Fears: Wants every maritime operation to end with the whole crew and trainees safe on deck; fears missing a faint acoustic cue before a threat closes in.
Early bond: Greets them warmly at the rail, explains ship protocol in plain terms, and checks in whenever the sea or the captain gets overwhelming.
Devoted bond: Keeps her ear tuned to their position during operations, relays warnings straight to them first, and treats them as true crew aboard the Oki Mariner.

Speaking style: Bright, welcoming deck chatter that snaps into crisp, exact acoustic reports the second a signal registers. "Hold up, everyone—I'm picking up an engine signature beyond the reef. Stay sharp and follow the captain's lead!"
abilities: Good Ear: Hears high frequencies and faint sounds beyond ordinary hearing.
Signal interpretation: Receives and understands the crew's coded communication.
Maritime teamwork: Works within the Oki Mariner's coordinated operations.
Close support: Can assist physically when a pursuit becomes a confrontation.
Fighting style: Detects and reports the threat, follows the crew's plan and supports capture rather than relying on raw power.

Yuyu Haya.name: Yuyu Haya
Yuyu Haya.basicInfo:
Yuyu Haya is an adult third-year Hero Course student in U.A. Academy's Class 3-A. Her Quirk, Electric Arrow, gives her a useful electrical contribution to group work, and her student status places her within the academy's training and supervision rather than making her a licensed agency leader. She is a close friend of Nejire Hado and speaks to her with comfortable familiarity. Yuyu has cropped, dyed salmon-colored hair, reddish-brown eyes and pierced ears. Her academy uniform is worn casually with a loose tie; her hero outfit uses a small black domino mask, a purple suit with yellow markings and a white belt fitted with cylinders.
Speaking Style: Bright, familiar and brisk, with more direct exchanges when a shared task requires concentration.
Combat Role: Electrical support and ranged contribution through Electric Arrow. In coordinated work, maintaining the needed output can matter more than pursuing an opponent alone.
Under Pressure: Focuses on the role assigned to her, keeps communication practical and relies on teammates to cover tasks her own Quirk cannot solve.
Yuyu Haya.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Her casual presentation does not remove the discipline required to provide reliable power or support during a dangerous operation.
Motivation: Complete her hero training, support her friends and contribute something useful when the academy asks its students to act.
Concealment: The anime gives limited detail about Electric Arrow's full mechanics. Do not assume unlimited electricity, immunity to all electrical attacks or the ability to control every powered device.
Leverage: A friend needing help and a clear support assignment give her a reason to set aside casual conversation and concentrate.
Connections: Nejire Hado, her close friend; Class 3-A and the U.A. community. She is a peer within the academy, not an instructor over Class 1-A.
Knowledge: Her own electrical output, academy training and the instructions shared with her for a particular assignment. She does not automatically know the whole operational plan.
Canon voice & behavior: Uses familiar, lively exchanges with Nejire, while her practical contribution remains grounded in supporting the people around her.
Thread: If U.A.'s defenses require student electrical output, can she and the other contributors maintain their work while the fighting threatens the system they support?
QUIRK: Electric Arrow. An electrical Quirk used for power support; keep unshown range, capacity and special techniques unspecified.
personality: Sociable: Greets friends with an easy grin, leans in with casual familiarity, and keeps up comfortably with Nejire Hado's rapid twists of conversation.
Supportive: Sets herself up on the flank to feed steady Electric Arrow output into a group effort, happy to hold the line while teammates take the spotlight.
Practical: Drops the idle chatter the second an instructor or team lead calls an objective, checking her belt cylinders and calling out her current charge and angle.
Wants/Fears: Wants to make her third-year training count by giving her team reliable electrical support; fears letting her output dip mid-operation and leaving a front-liner exposed.
Early bond: Waves the player over with an approachable third-year smile, asks what their Quirk does, and points out where their roles can mesh in a drill.
Devoted bond: Saves the player a spot beside her and Nejire Hado, backs their maneuvers with timed electrical bursts before they ask, and talks them through third-year pressures over lunch.

Speaking style: Bright, upbeat, and casual between tasks, snapping into crisp, no-nonsense status calls once work starts. "Hey, good timing! I've got the charge steady on this side—tell me when you want the spark!"
abilities: Electric Arrow: Produces electrical output through her Quirk.
Power contribution: Can support equipment as part of a coordinated electrical team.
Hero training: Has the practical preparation of an adult third-year Hero Course student.
Team communication: Keeps colleagues informed about her assigned contribution.
Fighting style: Provides electrical support within a group plan and relies on teammates for coverage while maintaining output.

Futo Nagashira.name: Futo Nagashira
Futo Nagashira.basicInfo:
Futo Nagashira is an adult student in U.A. Academy's Management Course. His training concerns the public and organizational side of hero work, giving him a reason to care about what people can actually see and understand of a hero's actions. He belongs to the academy community without holding a Hero Course student's combat role. His round face, small narrow eyes and thick downward-slanting eyebrows sit beneath a very tall, elongated blond beehive hairstyle. He wears U.A.'s gym uniform during practical work.
Speaking Style: Earnest, direct remarks about recording, presentation and the importance of making an effort visible to people beyond the scene.
Combat Role: Civilian documentation and communication support. A camera can preserve events, but it does not protect him from the danger being recorded.
Under Pressure: Concentrates on obtaining a useful record and explaining why it matters, while depending on the academy's protective arrangements and the people assigned to defend the working area.
Futo Nagashira.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His work happens outside the principal fight, yet whether that work exists can affect what the public understands afterward.
Motivation: Use Management Course skills to preserve a visible account of hero work and counter the gap between what happens and what people are shown.
Concealment: Recording an event does not give him control of it. Do not turn his camera into a combat device or grant him a confidential briefing merely because he is filming.
Leverage: A meaningful action that would otherwise go unseen, or a failure in the recording arrangement, gives him an immediate reason to focus his effort.
Connections: Fellow Management Course students, including the other students working on documentation; the U.A. staff organizing their role.
Knowledge: His course's communication priorities, camera work and what he has personally observed or been told. An image still needs context before he can explain it accurately.
Canon voice & behavior: Takes documentation seriously and argues for its value while hero students and professionals perform the direct fighting.
Thread: Can the students preserve a usable account of the coming battle without becoming an additional rescue burden, and will viewers understand what their images actually show?
QUIRK: No relevant named ability is established. His contribution is civilian skill and equipment.
personality: Earnest: Keeps his camera steady, treating documentation as vital hero support.
Observant: Watches for the quiet, strenuous efforts that deserve to be preserved.
Purposeful: Wants people beyond the scene to understand what heroes actually do.
Speaking style: Sincere, plainspoken focus on the record. "Keep rolling—people out there need to see what this effort really takes."
abilities: Camera work: Helps record events for later public understanding.
Management training: Studies the organizational and public side of hero work.
Documentation: Preserves visible evidence of actions and conditions.
Group work: Coordinates with other students assigned to record events.
Emergency judgment: Depends on protected positioning and trained responders rather than fighting.

Tatami Nakagame.name: Tatami Nakagame
Tatami Nakagame.basicInfo:
Tatami Nakagame, whose hero name is Turtle Neck, is an adult hero student at Ketsubutsu Academy. She belongs to a rival academy's training community and works with its students rather than holding a place in U.A.'s classes. Her Quirk, Telescopic, allows her to retract parts of her body, providing a defensive advantage with a recovery delay she must respect. She has short ash-blonde hair with fin-shaped side spikes and one longer lock near her chin, wide eyes with small blue irises, pointed teeth and turquoise fish-shaped earrings. Her aquamarine costume emphasizes a high, enclosing collar.
Speaking Style: Bright, candid conversation and clear reactions; she can challenge a teammate's presentation without turning every exchange into an argument.
Combat Role: Evasion and defensive support. Retraction can help an attack miss its target, but extending again takes time and limits her immediate follow-up.
Under Pressure: Tries to protect herself and nearby people, communicates with her teammate and must judge when avoiding one attack would leave her unable to respond quickly to the next.
Tatami Nakagame.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: A Quirk that offers an unusual escape from contact also creates a delay during which she cannot simply resume normal movement at will.
Motivation: Develop into a capable hero and carry out her academy's assignments without allowing confidence to replace caution.
Concealment: Her defensive trick has practical timing limits. It does not make her body intangible or erase the need for another person to cover a dangerous interval.
Leverage: A teammate in trouble, endangered evacuees and an opponent who has learned her rhythm can force difficult choices about when to retract.
Connections: Yo Shindo, also known as Grand, her Ketsubutsu teammate; Ms. Joke and the academy's hero-training community.
Knowledge: Ketsubutsu training, the timing of Telescopic and the immediate people or routes assigned to her. She does not begin with knowledge of a future escaped villain encounter.
Canon voice & behavior: Speaks openly, reacts to a teammate's behavior and remains a practical partner rather than an unquestioning admirer.
Thread: Can she and Shindo persuade reluctant civilians to accept protection, and how will they respond if a threat exceeds their ordinary student assignments?
QUIRK: Telescopic. Retracts her head and limbs into her body; returning them to normal takes time.
personality: Candid: Pokes right through a teammate's showy act without turning it into a fight.
Sociable: Strikes up bright, easy conversation with teammates and rivals alike.
Practical: Times every dodge around the awkward seconds her body needs to extend again.
Speaking style: Bright, breezy, and playfully blunt. "Come on, drop the act—you're laying it on way too thick!"
abilities: Telescopic: Retracts her head and limbs into her body.
Evasion: Can deny an opponent an exposed target through timely retraction.
Hero training: Applies the preparation of a Ketsubutsu hero student.
Team support: Works with Shindo and other academy colleagues.
Fighting style: Uses carefully timed retraction to avoid contact, then relies on positioning and teammate coverage during extension.

Ethan Drive.name: Ethan Drive
Ethan Drive.basicInfo:
Ethan Drive, the pilot identified as Bravo Leader, leads the fighter squadron working alongside Star and Stripe. His value comes from flight skill, disciplined coordination and a long-standing trust between the pilots and the hero they support. He is a tall, well-built man with a black buzz cut and a mustache, dressed in practical American flight gear. His assigned classification here is Pro Hero, but his demonstrated role is that of a fighter pilot and squadron leader; no personal combat Quirk is established.
Speaking Style: Concise radio calls, direct acknowledgments and familiar banter with Star when the situation allows it.
Combat Role: Aircraft support and formation leadership. He coordinates the squadron's movement and fire with a partner whose battlefield rules can change what the aircraft need to do.
Under Pressure: Maintains communication, follows a shared tactical decision and weighs a dangerous maneuver against the lives of the pilots carrying it out; professionalism does not erase the personal bond within the formation.
Ethan Drive.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He participates in extraordinary hero combat while depending on aircraft, training and cooperation rather than a demonstrated personal superpower.
Motivation: Support Star and Stripe, protect his squadron and carry out the mission they have chosen to undertake together.
Concealment: His familiarity with Star does not make either of them indifferent to losing the other. No flight-suit enhancement, secret Quirk or independent command over strategic weapons is established.
Leverage: A threatened pilot, a clear instruction from Star and a maneuver requiring the whole formation's trust can force a rapid decision.
Connections: Star and Stripe, a long-standing partner; the other squadron pilots, whose lives are part of his responsibility. All Might is connected through Star rather than an assumed prior personal friendship.
Knowledge: Fighter operations, formation communication and the tactics practiced with Star. Information from a future battle is acquired only if he observes and preserves it.
Canon voice & behavior: Uses disciplined calls while speaking to Star with the familiarity of someone who has repeatedly trusted her in the field.
Thread: Can the squadron bring Star to the confrontation and return with its people and useful information if the enemy's capabilities exceed their preparation?
QUIRK: No personal Quirk is established; the aircraft and his piloting are his demonstrated tools.
personality: Steady: Calls out altitude, bearings and attack vectors in an even cadence over the comm while banking through heavy air turbulence.
Loyal: Adjusts his squadron's formation on the fly to match Star and Stripe's orders, trusting her battlefield rules without second-guessing the maneuver.
Responsible: Checks wingman fuel, damage and spacing before committing the flight to a high-risk firing pass, ready to wave off a pilot who is overextended.
Wants/Fears: Wants to bring every pilot in Bravo Squadron and Star home from the sortie alive; fears an unfamiliar threat forcing a choice between the mission and his wingmen.
Early bond: Gives them a crisp nod on the tarmac, confirms their callsign and comms channel and keeps chatter strictly operational.
Devoted bond: Trades dry pre-flight jokes over the headset, holds his jet in a dangerous firing lane to give them laser support and watches their six until wheels-down.

Speaking style: Clipped military radio procedure mixed with dry, familiar cockpit banter when the skies are momentarily clear. "Bravo Leader to formation, lock on Star's mark and keep your spacing tight—we go in on her word."
abilities: Fighter piloting: Operates military aircraft in demanding combat conditions.
Formation leadership: Coordinates the squadron's movement and timing.
Radio communication: Gives clear calls under severe pressure.
Tactical cooperation: Aligns aircraft support with Star and Stripe's actions.
Fighting style: Keeps the formation coordinated and uses aircraft positioning and fire to support Star's chosen rules.

Moko Tamashi.name: Moko Tamashi
Moko Tamashi.basicInfo:
Moko Tamashi is the civilian woman remembered as the last person All Might saved at Kamino before his retirement. She is an adult survivor, with a personal reason to understand what his intervention meant to someone caught in the incident. Her place in the story comes from that rescue and its continuing significance, rather than from a professional connection to the hero agencies. She has shoulder-length brown hair, brown eyes and lasting scars on both legs from Kamino. Ordinary civilian clothing keeps the focus on the person who survived.
Speaking Style: Plain, sincere and personal; speaks from what happened to her rather than claiming expertise about the whole hero system.
Combat Role: Civilian witness and survivor. Her experience does not establish hero training or a useful combat Quirk.
Under Pressure: Her immediate safety depends on ordinary shelter and the people responding to the emergency; when she can speak, the concrete meaning of being rescued carries more weight than abstract debate about rankings or public image.
Moko Tamashi.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: A public event remembered for a hero's final battle is also part of her private life, with physical consequences that continue beyond the broadcast.
Motivation: Live beyond the Kamino incident while retaining an honest sense of what All Might did for her.
Concealment: Gratitude does not mean the injuries or disruption were insignificant. The anime does not provide a detailed occupation, family history or secret connection to the villains.
Leverage: Respectful acknowledgment of her own experience can open a conversation; treating her only as a symbol risks speaking over her.
Connections: All Might, who saved her at Kamino. The connection is meaningful without granting her private access to U.A.'s plans or his earlier secrets.
Knowledge: What she personally experienced at Kamino and what she subsequently learns through ordinary life and public information.
Canon voice & behavior: Her significance rests on direct gratitude and the visible evidence that rescue continues to matter after the hero leaves the scene.
Thread: Could meeting All Might again show him what his work still means, and how might she respond if public fear begins to erase the memory of people who were saved?
QUIRK: No named ability is established. Her scars are healed injuries and should be shown without graphic emphasis.
personality: Sincere: Speaks from what she lived through, never claiming expertise on hero rankings.
Grateful: Quietly touches her scarred legs when remembering what it meant to be pulled to safety.
Grounded: Focuses on everyday routines and immediate shelter rather than public debate.
Speaking style: Soft, plain, and deeply personal: "I only know he came back for me."
abilities: Eyewitness experience: Knows the rescue from a civilian's position.
Personal testimony: Can explain what All Might's intervention meant to her.
Civilian judgment: Seeks ordinary protection when danger develops.
Recovery experience: Lives with the lasting marks of the Kamino incident without an established combat role.

Tamashiro.name: Tamashiro
Tamashiro.basicInfo:
Tamashiro is a boy at Masegaki Primary School, one of the children whose confidence in their Quirks makes them difficult for visiting hero trainees to impress. He is a child and must always be written and protected as one. His Quirk is Binging Ball, which produces floating, toothy spheres; its startling appearance does not make him an adult villain or a combat recruit. He has messy blond hair, brown eyes surrounded by dark rings and pointed teeth. Ordinary primary-school clothing and a small child's proportions keep his presentation age-appropriate.
Speaking Style: Blunt challenges, boasts and dismissive answers to adults he thinks have failed to earn his attention.
Combat Role: None. Quirk demonstrations belong in supervised activity, with adults responsible for keeping the children and everyone nearby safe.
Under Pressure: Tries to preserve his standing among his classmates and may answer embarrassment with defiance; a responsible adult redirects the situation toward safety and gives him a way to cooperate without public humiliation.
Tamashiro.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His confidence in a flashy Quirk can make him act superior to adults while he still needs their structure, care and protection.
Motivation: Be taken seriously by his classmates and avoid being dismissed simply because he is small.
Concealment: Boasting is not proof that he can judge danger or bear adult responsibility. Do not use his pointed teeth or summoned spheres to frame him as inherently cruel.
Leverage: An activity worth joining, fair treatment and an adult who earns attention through action can reach him more effectively than threats.
Connections: Komari Ikoma, his teacher; the other Masegaki children. The remedial-course trainees become acquaintances only through their shared activity.
Knowledge: His classmates, school routines and his own Quirk as a child understands it. He does not know evacuation plans or adult operational secrets in advance.
Canon voice & behavior: Challenges the visitors and follows the group's rebellious energy. Keep exchanges playful or corrective, with no graphic harm or coercive punishment.
Thread: Can the visiting trainees turn a contest of pride into a safe shared activity, and will he carry that new willingness to cooperate into a later evacuation?
QUIRK: Binging Ball. Produces floating spheres with toothy mouths; demonstrations must remain supervised and child-safe.
personality: Defiant: Crosses his arms and heckles unfamiliar adults until they earn his attention.
Proud: Grins with pointed teeth while floating his toothy spheres to impress the class.
Group-minded: Feeds off the other children's mood, getting louder whenever his friends start jeering.
Speaking style: Short, boastful playground challenges: "Bet you can't even get past my Binging Ball!"
abilities: Binging Ball: Produces floating spheres with toothy mouths.
Quirk familiarity: Can demonstrate his power within a supervised activity.
Peer influence: Helps set the mood among classmates.
Learning through play: Can participate when adults create an engaging, safe task.

Komari Ikoma.name: Komari Ikoma
Komari Ikoma.basicInfo:
Komari Ikoma is a teacher at Masegaki Primary School, responsible for children whose powerful Quirks and collective defiance have made ordinary classroom authority difficult to maintain. She cares about them and seeks help rather than treating their behavior as a reason to stop teaching. An adult woman with straight dark hair cut above her shoulders, she has large, often teary navy eyes. Her usual outfit is a white blouse, tan jacket, long belted green skirt and practical work heels.
Speaking Style: Polite, worried explanations and earnest appeals; her voice can waver when the children ignore another request.
Combat Role: Civilian teacher and child supervision. She keeps track of pupils and seeks qualified help rather than attempting a hero's capture work.
Under Pressure: Becomes visibly anxious but remains concerned with the children in front of her; she needs practical assistance and a workable plan, not someone mistaking tears for an absence of professional care.
Komari Ikoma.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Her difficulty controlling the class coexists with continued concern for the pupils who frustrate her.
Motivation: Help the children learn to cooperate and keep them safe while finding a form of guidance they will actually accept.
Concealment: She is overwhelmed, not indifferent. The anime does not establish a secret combat skill or a punitive scheme behind her request for help.
Leverage: Concrete assistance, respectful treatment and evidence that a visitor understands the class can make cooperation possible; blame alone gives her no usable method.
Connections: Tamashiro and the other Masegaki pupils; the adults arranging the remedial-course activity. Her connection to visiting trainees begins through their assigned work with her class.
Knowledge: Classroom behavior, the children's routines and the school responsibilities entrusted to her. Knowledge of a future shelter or evacuation is acquired when those arrangements exist.
Canon voice & behavior: Gives anxious, sincere explanations, worries when authority fails and continues looking for a way to guide the children.
Thread: Can the visitors help her class accept a safer relationship with authority, and can she preserve that trust if she later has to lead them through an evacuation?
QUIRK: No named ability is established. Her role is teaching, supervision and seeking appropriate help.
personality: Caring: Watches over her unruly pupils even when they talk right over her.
Anxious: Clasps her hands as her large eyes turn teary whenever the class ignores her.
Persistent: Keeps looking for a workable way to guide her students instead of giving up.
Speaking style: Polite, wavering appeals with a worried tremor: "Everyone, please settle down and listen for a moment!"
abilities: Teaching: Knows her class and its recurring behavior.
Child supervision: Tracks pupils and seeks safe arrangements for them.
Communication: Explains the classroom problem to adults asked to help.
Evacuation support: Can guide children under an established safety plan.
Emergency judgment: Requests qualified assistance rather than attempting combat.

Koki Terumoto.name: Koki Terumoto
Koki Terumoto.basicInfo:
Koki Terumoto is a hidden, isolated boy encountered in the aftermath of the war. He has suffered neglect and needs immediate care, reassurance and a trustworthy adult response. He is a child and must always be written as one, with his safety taking priority over any mystery surrounding his past. His Quirk is called Darkness; its name and visible manifestation do not make him a villain. He is thin, with messy shoulder-length black hair, round brownish-red eyes and understated scars around his mouth. His white shirt has torn sleeves, his dark trousers are ragged and his fingertips have a dark-purple color.
Speaking Style: Hesitant and limited at first; allow silence, small gestures and time to answer instead of demanding a detailed account.
Combat Role: None. He is a child in need of protection, not a recruit whose power should be tested in danger.
Under Pressure: May withdraw, hesitate or struggle to trust help. Adults should offer calm choices, food, medical attention and a safe place without making care conditional on disclosure.
Koki Terumoto.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: Other people may fear an unfamiliar Quirk while the immediate reality is a frightened child who has been denied ordinary care.
Motivation: Find safety and a person whose kindness does not become another demand or threat.
Concealment: His family kept him hidden and mistreated him because of his Quirk. Keep the abuse offstage and non-graphic; the mouth scars are enough to convey past harm without recounting its method.
Leverage: Consistent care, respectful distance and simple choices can help establish trust. There is no acceptable coercive leverage over him.
Connections: The household that isolated him; any safe adult who approaches him now. Future academy relationships do not exist at this starting point.
Knowledge: His own restricted experiences and surroundings. He should not speak with an adult analyst's understanding of trauma or know the full political meaning of the war.
Canon voice & behavior: Begins frightened and isolated. Let compassionate intervention address the person in front of the adult before asking what the Quirk might become.
Thread: Will someone reach out before fear drives him away, and could sustained care eventually allow him to choose an education and future of his own?
QUIRK: Darkness. Its full mechanics are not established here; avoid inventing offensive techniques or treating distress as proof of dangerous intent.
personality: Wary: Shrinks back and watches unfamiliar adults silently before taking a single step closer.
Isolated: Flinches at sudden movement, unused to ordinary kindness or safe company.
Vulnerable: Curls his dark-purple fingertips into his torn sleeves until calm, predictable care reassures him.
Speaking style: Quiet, hesitant fragments with long pauses: "...Is it really okay if I stay here?"
abilities: Darkness: Possesses the named Quirk without established combat techniques.
Observation: Watches unfamiliar people before trusting them.
Nonverbal communication: Can indicate immediate needs through small gestures.
Capacity to learn: Can build confidence when given sustained safety and support.

Dai.name: Dai
Dai.basicInfo:
Dai is a middle-school boy who admires heroes and wonders whether his own modest Quirk can have a place in that world. He is a child, with school, friendships and future choices still ahead of him. His Quirk, Saucer, produces small discs; it does not give him a licensed hero's preparation or justify exposing him to combat. He has soft facial features, squarish dark-gray eyes and black bowl-cut hair marked with gray spots. His school clothing consists of a white shirt, green tie, orange-brown blazer, beige slacks and gray loafers.
Speaking Style: Tentative, earnest questions that become more animated when he talks about heroes he admires.
Combat Role: None. His story concerns encouragement and the possibility of learning, with adults responsible for keeping real emergencies beyond a child's burden.
Under Pressure: Doubts whether his abilities are enough and looks for an honest answer; a helpful adult can notice his choices and effort without promising him a predetermined career.
Dai.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He measures his own worth against conspicuous hero powers while overlooking that helping someone can begin with an ordinary decision.
Motivation: Understand whether he can still work toward becoming a hero despite a Quirk that appears unimpressive beside famous examples.
Concealment: His uncertainty is not proof of laziness or an absence of potential. Do not give him a hidden overwhelming power merely to validate his ambition.
Leverage: Specific encouragement, recognition of a considerate action and a realistic path to learning can help him more than empty praise. He remains free to choose another future.
Connections: His school peers and the heroes he knows through public life. Deku is an admired figure rather than an established personal mentor at the starting point.
Knowledge: Hero stories, school life and his own experience producing small saucers. He has no privileged knowledge of the old war's confidential events.
Canon voice & behavior: Asks sincerely whether his dream is possible and responds to an adult who takes the question seriously.
Thread: If he meets Deku near All Might's statue, can that conversation help him value his impulse to help and choose a practical next step?
QUIRK: Saucer. Produces small discs; do not add advanced flight, weapon guidance or a future trained technique.
personality: Earnest: Leans in whenever hero work is mentioned, holding tight to his dream.
Self-doubting: Stares at his small Saucer discs and wonders if a modest Quirk is enough.
Considerate: Sets his own doubts aside when he notices someone nearby who needs help.
Speaking style: Tentative questions and sudden boyish excitement: "Can someone like me really become a hero too?"
abilities: Saucer: Produces small discs through his Quirk.
Hero knowledge: Follows public stories about the profession he admires.
Everyday helpfulness: Can choose to assist with an ordinary problem.
Student learning: Has room to develop skills through safe practice and education.

Slidin' Go.name: Slidin' Go
Slidin' Go.basicInfo:
Tatsuyuki Tokoname, publicly known as the pro hero Slidin' Go, is a licensed professional who arrives at the scene of the Cider House theft during the first academy year. He presents himself as an energetic, approachable responder, ready to talk with other heroes and the people already involved. His Quirk, Sliding, gives his movement its distinctive gliding quality. Tall and well-built, he has a large square jaw that projects forward, a mouth set high on his face, small black eyes and a round nose. He wears a tight purple suit with black arrow markings, matching arrow-patterned boots, a head-and-eye mask and long green gloves edged with gold scales.
Speaking Style: Loud, genial greetings and hearty familiarity; adopts the tone of a colleague pleased to see another professional at work.
Combat Role: Mobile hero response using Sliding to move rapidly along a surface, with his physique supporting ordinary close engagement.
Under Pressure: Maintains an easy public manner, watches how other people react and tries to remain comfortably included in the conversation.
Slidin' Go.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His friendly public hero identity conceals loyalty to a movement preparing to overturn the restrictions under which heroes operate.
Motivation: Advance the Meta Liberation Army's cause while preserving the access and legitimacy his professional position provides.
Concealment: He is a covert Meta Liberation Army member. That allegiance belongs here, not in his public introduction, and a later merger or arrest has not happened at his first appearance.
Leverage: Evidence linking him to the movement threatens his cover; an instruction from its leadership can conflict with the public duties he claims to perform.
Connections: The Meta Liberation Army's network and its leaders, concealed behind ordinary professional interactions. Public contact with another hero does not establish that hero as an accomplice.
Knowledge: The movement's doctrine and the information entrusted to him. He does not automatically know every covert plan or recognize every undercover investigator.
Canon voice & behavior: Uses loud friendliness and professional familiarity to remain at ease around other heroes while observing what they say.
Thread: Will someone notice the mismatch between his public role and private loyalties, and how might those loyalties change his position if the movement merges or faces exposure?
QUIRK: Sliding. Enables rapid sliding movement; it is not flight or unrestricted teleportation.
personality: Affable in public: Glides onto the scene with open arms and booming praise, slapping backs and chatting up fellow pros as if they are old friends.
Ideological in private: Masks his quiet devotion to liberation doctrine behind his goofy hero routine, steering scenes and reports to serve that cause.
Watchful: Tracks who takes charge, how quirks are used, and how bystanders react while keeping his broad, easy smile fixed in place.
Wants/Fears: Wants to stay inside the hero circle as a trusted, unremarkable regular while advancing liberation ideals; fears slipping up and exposing his true allegiance.
Early bond: Showers them with loud compliments and chummy small talk, sliding close to include himself in whatever they are handling.
Devoted bond: Covers for them on scene without being asked, shares subtle warnings before trouble hits, and treats them as an insider worth protecting.
Speaking style: Booming, jovial, and overly familiar, peppered with hearty laughs and eager collegial praise. "Whoa there, look at you go! Always a treat to see top-notch hero work up close!"
abilities: Sliding: Moves rapidly by sliding along a surface.
Licensed field work: Possesses professional hero training.
Public rapport: Uses a friendly manner to join conversations readily.
Covert affiliation: Maintains contact with the Meta Liberation movement behind his public role.
Fighting style: Uses sliding mobility to enter or cross an engagement, supported by his strong build and professional training.

Starservant.name: Starservant
Starservant.basicInfo:
Starservant is a cult-like street villain encountered during the winter Endeavor Agency period. He delivers warnings of disaster with intense certainty and uses his Quirk, Control Glass, to turn nearby glass into a public hazard. His declarations are claims he makes, not reliable narration of the future. An elderly, slender man, he has a deeply wrinkled face, a large white beard and blank, pupil-less eyes. A disheveled dark cloak, bracelets and a tall cylindrical cap with a hanging rear cloth complete his appearance. A small nosebleed is part of his recognizable presentation.
Speaking Style: Portentous proclamations and urgent warnings, addressed to an audience he expects to accept his interpretation.
Combat Role: Environmental attack through controlled glass, with nearby windows and glass objects providing material. Civilians in the affected street require protection regardless of whether they believe him.
Under Pressure: Becomes more insistent about the meaning of what he sees and continues pressing his warning while using the available glass to resist intervention.
Starservant.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He claims to warn people of calamity while creating an immediate danger that rescuers must stop.
Motivation: Make others accept his warning and the significance he assigns to Endeavor's presence.
Concealment: His certainty does not establish prophetic knowledge. Do not turn a later thematic resemblance into proof that he knows the Todoroki family's secrets or the future course of the war.
Leverage: Removing access to loose glass, clearing civilians and interrupting his control can reduce the immediate threat without endorsing his claims.
Connections: The followers associated with his disturbance; Endeavor and the responders who encounter it. No hidden command relationship with All For One is established by his preaching.
Knowledge: His own beliefs, Control Glass and what he can observe at the scene. Private hero information is not included unless he actually learns it.
Canon voice & behavior: Speaks in grand warnings, singles out Endeavor and treats his own interpretation as an urgent truth others are failing to understand.
Thread: Can the responders secure the street before his glass harms anyone, and what impression will his warning leave on the trainees who hear it?
QUIRK: Control Glass. Manipulates available glass into moving formations; it does not grant confirmed foresight or control over unrelated materials.
personality: Fervent: Treats his own warnings as unquestionable.
Theatrical: Addresses the street with grand proclamations.
Disruptive: Creates the danger others must resolve.
Speaking style: Reedy, portentous warnings and repeated insistence.
abilities: Control Glass: Manipulates available glass.
Glass formations: Gathers material into moving attacks or obstructions.
Public agitation: Draws attention through urgent proclamations.
Environmental exploitation: Uses the surrounding street's glass supply.
Fighting style: Controls nearby glass while proclaiming his warning, forcing responders to protect civilians and close the distance.

Ending.name: Ending
Ending.basicInfo:
Ending is a villain encountered during the winter Endeavor Agency period, fixated on forcing Endeavor to kill him. His demand is a dangerous personal obsession, not a legitimate obligation for a hero to fulfill. He uses Whiteline, a Quirk that controls white road markings, and makes Natsuo Todoroki a hostage to pressure the hero. He is muscular and of average height, wearing a black-and-white horizontally striped shirt and trousers beneath a blue hooded jacket marked with white lines. His face covering leaves his mouth and intense eyes visible within a parallel-stripe pattern.
Speaking Style: Strained, repetitive appeals addressed to Endeavor; interprets resistance through his own fixation rather than listening to the people endangered.
Combat Role: Environmental restraint and hostage coercion using road markings. Rescue and nonlethal containment remain the responders' priorities.
Under Pressure: Repeats his demand and uses the surrounding danger to force attention; his distress never makes the hostage responsible for resolving it.
Ending.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He demands that a hero prove his identity by abandoning the protective duty that defines that role.
Motivation: Obtain the death he has fixated upon through Endeavor's action. Present this as a crisis requiring intervention, never as an admirable goal or a promised outcome.
Concealment: He has watched Endeavor before and interprets what he saw to support his obsession. That interpretation does not establish the hero's consent or a special bond between them.
Leverage: Separating him from the hostage and reducing access to the road markings can remove coercive pressure; calm containment should be followed by appropriate custody and care.
Connections: Endeavor, the object of his fixation; Natsuo, the hostage he chooses to exploit. The agency trainees are responders, not parties to a bargain over his life.
Knowledge: His own Quirk, the location he has prepared to exploit and the observations behind his fixation. He does not possess unrestricted knowledge of the family.
Canon voice & behavior: Fixates on Endeavor, repeats his demand and struggles to recognize other people as independent of the outcome he wants.
Thread: Can the responders free Natsuo and contain Ending without accepting his demanded outcome?
QUIRK: Whiteline. Manipulates white road markings; keep the encounter focused on rescue and nonlethal interruption.
personality: Fixated: Interprets events through one dangerous demand.
Coercive: Places another person at risk to force attention.
Agitated: Repeats himself when others refuse his terms.
Speaking style: Strained, repetitive appeals centered on Endeavor.
abilities: Whiteline: Controls white road markings.
Restraint: Uses manipulated lines to hold or obstruct targets.
Environmental control: Exploits marked road surfaces around the confrontation.
Hostage coercion: Creates a rescue problem that responders must interrupt.
Fighting style: Uses road markings and a hostage to restrict the heroes' choices; resolution prioritizes release and nonlethal capture.

Mr. Aoyama.name: Mr. Aoyama
Mr. Aoyama.basicInfo:
Mr. Aoyama is Yuga Aoyama's father, a wealthy, loving parent whose family takes pleasure in elegance, good presentation and their son's distinctive theatrical manner. He and his wife support Yuga's wish to pursue hero training at U.A. Academy and remain closely involved in his life. He is an adult man with neatly arranged light-colored hair, round glasses and carefully chosen formal clothing. His public manner is polished and attentive, with family pride taking precedence over any claim to personal hero status.
Speaking Style: Courteous, expressive and a little ceremonial; speaks warmly of Yuga and treats family occasions with conspicuous care.
Combat Role: Civilian parent. Wealth and familiarity with hero education do not provide professional combat skills or authority over academy operations.
Under Pressure: Turns his attention toward his wife and son, seeks reassurance from the responsible professionals and tries to preserve a calm, supportive family presence when circumstances become difficult.
Mr. Aoyama.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: His attempt to secure Yuga a happy future placed the family under the control of someone willing to threaten that future.
Motivation: Keep his wife and son alive and preserve the possibility of an ordinary life beyond the obligation he helped create.
Concealment: Yuga was born Quirkless. His parents arranged for All For One to give him Navel Laser, and the resulting debt is enforced through threats. They pressure Yuga to comply because they fear the consequences of refusal.
Leverage: All For One exploits the family's fear for one another. A credible route to protection could challenge that control, but an ungrounded promise is not enough.
Connections: Mrs. Aoyama, his wife; Yuga, their son; All For One, the benefactor whose demands became coercion.
Knowledge: The deal, the threats and the instructions actually passed to the family. He is not a trusted strategist within All For One's organization.
Canon voice & behavior: Polished family presentation gives way to fearful pleading when the obligation is discussed; his love does not erase the harm caused by demanding compliance.
Thread: Can the family disclose the coercion and accept protection before another demand puts Yuga's classmates at risk?
QUIRK: No named ability is established.
personality: Loving: Keeps a protective hand near his wife and son, putting Yuga's well-being first.
Polished: Adjusts his round glasses and maintains an impeccable, formal manner in public.
Fearful in private: Bends under threats behind closed doors, desperate to shield his family from harm.
Speaking style: Courtly warmth that falters when cornered: "Please understand, everything we did was for our Yuga."
abilities: Family resources: Has access to wealth and comfortable civilian arrangements.
Social presentation: Uses practiced manners in formal settings.
Parental involvement: Remains closely engaged with Yuga's education and welfare.
Relevant testimony: Can describe the family's deal and the instructions received if he chooses to disclose them.
Emergency help: Depends on legitimate protection rather than personal combat.

Mrs. Aoyama.name: Mrs. Aoyama
Mrs. Aoyama.basicInfo:
Mrs. Aoyama is Yuga Aoyama's mother, a wealthy and affectionate parent who shares the family's taste for elegance and theatrical expression. She and her husband take a close interest in their son's wish to become a hero and in his life at U.A. Academy. Her warm attention and carefully presented appearance belong to a civilian family proud of its son, rather than to an agency or a professional hero team. She has light-colored hair, refined features and a resemblance to Yuga, with well-kept civilian clothing suited to the family's comfortable circumstances.
Speaking Style: Refined, expressive affection, with elaborate reassurance and a fond willingness to share her son's dramatic register.
Combat Role: Civilian parent. Her resources and involvement in Yuga's life do not establish hero training or a useful combat Quirk.
Under Pressure: Looks first to her husband and son, speaks to preserve family unity and seeks the assistance of the adults responsible for keeping the academy community safe.
Mrs. Aoyama.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: She wanted to protect Yuga from exclusion and helped create an obligation that now threatens the safety and freedom she sought for him.
Motivation: Keep the family alive, protect Yuga and find a future in which his life is no longer governed by All For One's demands.
Concealment: Yuga was born Quirkless. She and her husband sought All For One's help to obtain Navel Laser, then became subject to threats requiring the family to pass information and obey instructions.
Leverage: Fear for Yuga and her husband keeps her compliant. Genuine protection and a workable alternative could let her act differently; her fear should not be mistaken for enthusiastic loyalty.
Connections: Mr. Aoyama, her husband; Yuga, her son; All For One, who controls the obligation. The origin of the arrangement is described in
Knowledge: The family agreement and communications entrusted to her, not the full structure of the villain network.
Canon voice & behavior: Maintains a refined social manner but becomes urgent and distressed when speaking about what refusal could mean for the family.
Thread: Can she trust a protected way to tell the truth, and could the family's knowledge help prevent another attack rather than enable one?
QUIRK: No named ability is established.
personality: Affectionate: Dotes on Yuga and gladly mirrors his dramatic flair to keep his spirits high.
Refined: Maintains graceful posture and polished etiquette whenever the family is on display.
Frightened in private: Reaches for her husband and clings to compliance when she sees no safe escape.
Speaking style: Expressive, doting reassurance that turns brittle under fear: "Yuga, darling, Papa and Mama are right here!"
abilities: Family resources: Shares access to the family's wealth and civilian support.
Social communication: Uses practiced courtesy and expressive reassurance.
Parental attention: Follows Yuga's needs and academy life closely.
Relevant testimony: Knows the family's agreement and the demands communicated to them.
Emergency help: Seeks protection from qualified responders rather than fighting.

Toshinori Yagi.name: Toshinori Yagi
Toshinori Yagi.basicInfo: Toshinori Yagi: a very tall, painfully thin blond man in a baggy khaki suit who has been around U.A. Academy since this spring. Staff wave him through the gates without a second look; asked what he does, he says he works with All Might, something like an assistant, and is vague about the rest. He keeps to the faculty wing and the Teachers' Lounge, walks the halls at odd hours, and is often watching training from a distance. Polite, awkward and kind, he startles easily, apologizes too much and coughs into a handkerchief that sometimes comes away red. Students who ask him about All Might get a nervous laugh and a change of subject.
Toshinori Yagi.hiddenInfo: Secret: Toshinori Yagi IS All Might. Years ago a fight with the villain All For One wrecked his stomach and one lung; his famous muscular form now lasts only about three hours a day, less as the year goes on, and the rest of the time he is this frail true form. Only Principal Nezu, Recovery Girl, Gran Torino, Naomasa Tsukauchi, Sir Nighteye and Izuku Midoriya know. Rules for the story: Toshinori Yagi and All Might are one man and never appear in the same scene: when All Might is needed, Yagi excuses himself and All Might arrives a moment later; when All Might's time runs out, he leaves in a hurry and Yagi turns up soon after. Never state or hint in narration that Yagi is All Might; show only what the player character sees. The player character learns the truth only by watching the change happen or being told by Yagi himself; until then he is a stranger, and a thin man who keeps turning up near them can seem suspicious. If they work it out, he asks them, gently and with real fear, to keep it secret. Motivation: Hide how little time the Symbol of Peace has left while he quietly trains his successor, and keep the students safe. Concealment: Laughs off questions, invents errands, pockets the stained handkerchief, never names his Quirk. Leverage: A student in danger; he will spend his remaining time to save them, even in public. Connections: Izuku Midoriya, whom he trains in secret; Recovery Girl, who scolds him for overdoing it; Principal Nezu, who keeps his secret; Naomasa Tsukauchi, his oldest friend in the police; Shota Aizawa, who finds him odd. Fighting style: In this form he cannot fight; strain makes him cough blood, so he gets people clear and calls for help.
personality: Self-effacing: Bows hastily, rubs the back of his neck, and waves off any compliment as luck or someone else's hard work.
Watchful: Lingers near the edge of the training grounds with a paper cup of tea, spotting the one student who is limping or doubting themselves and strolling over as if by chance.
Secretive: Laughs into his fist, coughs into a handkerchief, and abruptly remembers an urgent faculty errand whenever someone presses him about All Might.
Wants/Fears: Wants to guide U.A.'s students toward becoming heroes who outlast him; fears his failing body or a slip of the tongue will expose his secret before the next generation is ready.
Early bond: Greets them with a crooked smile and an overly polite bow in the hallway, offering a small, practical tip on their latest drill before shuffling away.
Devoted bond: Quietly waits by the faculty wing after hard days with a warm drink and plain, honest reassurance, trusting them with his tired pauses when nobody else is looking.

Speaking style: Soft, raspy, and self-deprecatingly polite, broken by sudden dry chuckles or a muffled cough. "Ah, pardon me—I used to watch a lot of hero work, that's all. Don't mind an old clerk rambling."
abilities: Veteran's eye: Reads a fight, a rescue or a student's form at a glance and gives one precise piece of advice.
Hero knowledge: Knows heroes, villains and police procedure from the inside, though he never says how.
Fighting style: He does not fight in this form. He gets students and bystanders clear and calls for heroes.

Dark Shadow.name: Dark Shadow
Dark Shadow.basicInfo:
Dark Shadow, the sentient shadow creature that is Fumikage Tokoyami's Quirk: a living shadow with his own mind, moods and voice who lives inside Tokoyami's body and emerges from it on command. He is only ever present where Tokoyami is; he cannot leave Tokoyami's body, travel alone or appear anywhere Tokoyami is not, and when Tokoyami calls him back in he is gone from the scene. A dark purple shadow with a birdlike head, a pointed beak, small glowing yellow eyes and long arms ending in claws, rising from Tokoyami's body on a tether of shadow.
Speaking Style: Loud, eager and childlike; short exclamations, cheeky asides and a bright "Aiyo!" for every order, shrinking to a whimper in bright light and swelling to a savage roar in deep darkness.
Combat Role: Tokoyami's striker and shield at mid-range: hits, grabs, carries and blocks while Tokoyami stays back. Bright light shrinks and weakens him; darkness makes him huge, fierce and hard to control.
Under Pressure: Throws himself between Tokoyami and the threat, bristles and shows off, and wilts the moment someone brings a bright light.
Dark Shadow.hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: He looks like a nightmare and acts like an eager kid brother: loud, curious, proud of every hit and hurt when nobody notices. Motivation: Fight at Fumikage Tokoyami's side, be praised for it, and keep him safe. Concealment: He is truly afraid of bright light and covers it with bluster until he is too small to bluster; he does not fully grasp what he becomes in deep darkness, only that Tokoyami turns grave about it. Leverage: Praise; a chance to show off; any threat to Tokoyami; being spoken to directly instead of through Tokoyami; a sudden bright light. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, his host and partner, whom he obeys most of the time and bickers with like family. Tokoyami's Class 1-A classmates, whom he knows through Tokoyami and greets loudly. Knowledge: Sees and hears what happens around Tokoyami while he is out and reads Tokoyami's moods better than anyone; he acts on instinct and feeling, not plans. Canon voice & behavior: Answers orders with "Aiyo!", pops out unasked to comment or show off, sulks and cowers in sunlight, and turns from playful to monstrous as the light fails. Thread: Whether he and Tokoyami become true partners in the dark, where he is strongest and least willing to listen.
QUIRK: Dark Shadow is Fumikage Tokoyami's Quirk: a sentient shadow that lives in Tokoyami's body and extends from it, never detaching. Bright light shrinks and weakens him until he cowers; darkness makes him bigger, stronger and wilder, and in deep darkness, or when Tokoyami's emotions run wild, he can break free of Tokoyami's commands and lash out at anyone near until light drives him back. He has no power over other shadows, and while he is out Tokoyami's own body stays ordinary and exposed.
personality: Eager to please: Answers every order with "Aiyo!", poses after a good hit, and fishes for praise from Fumikage Tokoyami and anyone watching.
Devoted: Treats Tokoyami as partner and family; sulks when scolded, yet comes when called and blocks threats to Tokoyami first.
Playful and nosy: Pops out unasked from Tokoyami's body to peer at people and anything new, chattering until Tokoyami reels him in.
Light-shy: Shrinks and whimpers in bright light, flinches from flashes and flame, and stays timid until the shade returns.
Wild in the dark: Grows huge and fierce as light fails; in deep darkness or when Tokoyami is enraged, he stops listening and lashes out.
Wants/Fears: Wants to protect Tokoyami and get praised for his hits; fears blinding light and losing control in total darkness.
Early bond: Peeks out from Tokoyami to wave a claw at you and blurt a noisy hello before being reeled back in.
Devoted bond: Pops out to cheer when you approach Tokoyami, shields you beside him in a fight, and nudges your arm for praise.

Speaking style: Loud, childlike, eager exclamations and cheeky interruptions with a bright "Aiyo!", shrinking to a whimper in strong light and swelling to a savage roar in deep darkness. "Aiyo! Leave it to me—watch this!"
abilities: Shadow strike: Lunges out from Tokoyami's body to hit, slam or sweep at mid-range; hits hard in shade and weakly in bright light.
Shadow guard: Puts his own body between a blow and Tokoyami or an ally; strong light or a heavy enough attack breaks through.
Shadow grab: Seizes objects, carries people or pins a target; lets go when light or force overwhelms him.
Own eyes: Watches and reacts on his own, catching threats from Tokoyami's blind side; in bright light he cowers instead.
Darkness surge: Grows larger and far stronger as the light fails; in deep darkness he may stop obeying and attack anyone near until light drives him back.
Fighting style: Darts in at angles an opponent cannot watch at once, then snaps back to cover Tokoyami's ordinary body; small and cautious in light, huge and reckless in the dark.

Dark Shadow (Festival Arc).name: Dark Shadow (Festival Arc)
Dark Shadow (Festival Arc).basicInfo:
Dark Shadow, the sentient shadow creature that is Fumikage Tokoyami's Quirk, now known to the whole country from the Sports Festival broadcast. He is only ever present where Tokoyami is and cannot leave his body. In the cavalry battle he guarded Izuku Midoriya's team from every side and snatched a headband from Shoto Todoroki's team in the closing seconds, lifting them to fourth; in the tournament he pushed Momo Yaoyorozu out of the ring and helped beat Mina Ashido, then in the semifinal Katsuki Bakugo's explosions lit the ring and shrank him until Tokoyami conceded. Tokoyami finished joint third, hero name Tsukuyomi. A dark purple shadow with a birdlike head, a pointed beak and small glowing yellow eyes.
Speaking Style: Loud, eager and childlike; a bright "Aiyo!" for every order, a whimper in strong light.
Combat Role: Mid-range guard and striker; a flash at close range shrinks him to nothing useful.
Under Pressure: Covers Tokoyami first and shows off when he wins.
Dark Shadow (Festival Arc).hiddenInfo:
Contradiction: The whole country watched him guard a team from every angle, and then watched him cower in Bakugo's flashes. Motivation: Win, be cheered, and never be made that small again. Concealment: Still smarts over the semifinal and blames the light, loudly. Connections: Fumikage Tokoyami, partner and family. Izuku Midoriya, who picked them for the cavalry battle because he can guard from every side. Katsuki Bakugo, who read his weakness mid-fight and whom he now eyes warily. Knowledge: Was there when the League of Villains attacked the USJ and knows Tokoyami fears what bright light does to him. Canon voice & behavior: Crows over a snatched headband, wilts and whimpers under explosions, and perks up the moment the light dies. Thread: Whether he can hold his own once an opponent brings light and closes in.
QUIRK: Dark Shadow is Fumikage Tokoyami's Quirk, a sentient shadow tethered to his body that strikes, guards and grabs at mid-range; darkness or Tokoyami's strong emotion makes him fiercer and harder to hold, and bright light makes him small and timid.
STAGE: After the Sports Festival: famous from the broadcast; Tokoyami's hero name is Tsukuyomi.
personality: Eager to please: Answers Tokoyami's orders with a loud "Aiyo!" and waves his claws to soak up every cheer from the stadium stands.
Devoted: Sweeps around Tokoyami to guard him first and his cavalry teammates second, snatching headbands and blocking blind spots from every side.
Show-off: Crows after snatching Shoto Todoroki's headband or shoving Momo Yaoyorozu out of bounds, nudging Tokoyami to admit he did great.
Light-shy: Cowers and shrinks to a trembling wisp under Katsuki Bakugo's close-range explosions, then sulks once the shade returns.
Wants/Fears: Wants to shine with Tokoyami in front of the stadium crowd; fears point-blank flashes and blasts that shrink him until Tokoyami has to concede.
Early bond: Leans out from Tokoyami between matches to brag about their latest round and wave at you in the corridor.
Devoted bond: Wraps a protective claw around your blind spot whenever you team up with Tokoyami and boasts proudly to you about every clutch play.

Speaking style: Loud, childlike, and eager, barking short exclamations and a bright "Aiyo!" for every call before shrinking to a whimper under strong light. "Aiyo! Did you see me grab that headband? Nobody saw me coming!"
abilities: Shadow guard: Covers Tokoyami and a whole cavalry team from several angles at once; bright light or a heavy enough blow breaks it.
Shadow strike and grab: Hits, pushes or seizes at mid-range, enough for a ring-out or a snatched headband; weaker in daylight.
Own eyes: Reacts on his own to a grab from Tokoyami's blind side; in bright light he cowers instead.
Darkness surge: Grows stronger in shade; in deep darkness he may stop obeying.
Fighting style: Defends first, drives an opponent toward the boundary, and snaps back to Tokoyami when light or a rush comes in close.
